area: Protocol design (Protocol v1 schemas + architecture docs 03/04/05/06/07/16)
summary: All 5 shipped schemas parse and pass Draft 2020-12 meta-schema validation, and the conceptual decomposition (contract → receipt → bundle → verdict) is sound. But the protocol is not yet a protocol: 7 of the 11 types FPV-02 itself declares required have no schema (including AuthorityPolicy, ErrorEnvelope, ActorIdentity, CapabilityManifest); the versioning story is self-contradictory (`additionalProperties: false` everywhere makes the stated "unknown optional fields survive round-trip" rule impossible, so minor/patch evolution is breaking by construction); and Invariant 5 plus every ground-truth gate in 06 is unenforced — an EvidenceBundle with empty-string SHAs, an empty changed-path set and zero criteria validates with 0 errors. There is no canonical-JSON/hash algorithm, no digest chain between verdict and bundle, no fixture corpus, and the wire format drops `congruence` even though the R_eff formula in 06 and 145 of 148 existing evidence artifacts depend on it.

findings.claim: The versioning/compatibility story is a word, not a mechanism: every schema sets `additionalProperties: false` at every level, which makes the pack's own stated rule "unknown optional fields must survive round-trip" impossible and turns every minor/patch addition into a breaking change for older validators.
findings.evidence: 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:20-24 — "patch — совместимые исправления и новые optional fields; ... unknown optional fields должны сохраняться при round-trip". FPV-02.md:41 AC — "Unknown optional fields survive supported round-trips where required." Contradicted by work-contract.schema.json:6 `"additionalProperties": false` (also execution-receipt:6, evidence-bundle:6, verification-verdict:6, extension-manifest:6, plus every nested object). Empirical: adding the doc-mandated `trace_id` to a valid contract → `contract + unknown optional field trace_id -> 1 errors: Additional properties are not allowed ('trace_id' was unexpected)`. Compounding: `$id` is major-only (`work-contract.v1.json`), so 1.0 and 1.9 share one schema URL and a consumer cannot fetch the schema matching a `protocol_version` it received.
findings.recommendation: Decide the compatibility model explicitly and encode it: either (a) drop `additionalProperties: false` on the outer envelope and constrain only known fields, with an explicit `x-`/`extensions` namespace for vendor data and a documented preserve-on-round-trip requirement in the Rust DTOs (`#[serde(flatten)] HashMap` capture), or (b) keep strict validation and state honestly that ANY field addition is a major bump — which kills the "minor = compatible extension" rule. Also add minor-resolvable schema IDs (`work-contract.v1.0.json` + a `v1` alias) so a consumer can validate against the exact declared `protocol_version`.

findings.claim: Invariant 5 and every ground-truth gate in 06-EVIDENCE are unenforced by evidence-bundle.schema.json — a code-claiming bundle with empty-string base/result SHAs, an empty changed-path set, an empty delta digest and zero criteria validates cleanly.
findings.evidence: 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:107 — "Для code-claiming Evidence обязательны base SHA и result SHA." 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:54 — "code-claiming Evidence с пустым relevant delta не проходит". Schema evidence-bundle.schema.json:59-85 requires the four repository keys but attaches NO `minLength`, NO `pattern`, and NO constraint that base≠result; `criteria` (line 86-88) has no `minItems`; `commands` (line 137) is not in `required`. Empirical run against the schema: `EMPTY-SHA/EMPTY-DELTA/ZERO-CRITERIA bundle errors: 0` and `base==result, kind=vibes, provenance={} errors: 0`.
findings.recommendation: Add `pattern: "^[0-9a-f]{7,64}$"` (or `minLength: 7`) to `base_sha`/`result_sha`, `minLength` to `delta_digest`, `minItems: 1` to `criteria`, and express the code-claiming case structurally (e.g. an `if/then` on a `claims_code: true` discriminator requiring non-empty `changed_paths` and `base_sha != result_sha` — the inequality needs an engine assertion plus a schema-level `not: {const}` workaround, and must be listed explicitly as an engine-side gate in 06 so it is not assumed to be schema-covered). Note the same laxity in work-contract.schema.json:85-88 where `base_sha` has `minLength: 7` — the two documents disagree on how strict a SHA is.

findings.claim: Seven of the eleven protocol types FPV-02 declares required have no schema at all, and the most load-bearing one — AuthorityPolicy — is replaced by a hardcoded 4-key object in WorkContract that can express only 4 of the 13 actions 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY defines.
findings.evidence: FPV-02.md:16-26 lists 11 required types: ArtifactReference, ActorIdentity, Claim/Lease reference, WorkContract, ExecutionReceipt, EvidenceBundle, VerificationVerdict, AuthorityPolicy, ExternalReference, CapabilityManifest, ErrorEnvelope. `find protocol/schemas -type f` returns only work-contract, execution-receipt, evidence-bundle, verification-verdict, extension-manifest — so ArtifactReference, ActorIdentity, Claim/Lease, AuthorityPolicy, ExternalReference, CapabilityManifest and ErrorEnvelope are missing (extension-manifest is a 5th schema not on the list). 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:28-37 additionally names Claim and "lifecycle events" as Protocol members. 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:19-33 defines 13 actions (artifact.create … deployment.authorize) and 8 actor roles; work-contract.schema.json:214-248 hardcodes exactly `execute`, `expand_scope`, `accept_evidence`, `activate` with `additionalProperties: false`, so `decision.bind`, `evidence.dismiss`, `merge.approve`, `deployment.authorize` and 5 others cannot be carried. Roles are `items: {type: string}` — no enum, so `human_principal` and `typo_principal` are equally valid.
findings.recommendation: Ship the missing schemas in FPV-02 before FPV-03/05/07 start (they all depend on FPV-02). At minimum: an `authority-policy.v1.schema.json` keyed by the 13 actions with an actor-role enum, an `error-envelope.v1.schema.json` with a closed error-code registry (16-CONFORMANCE.md:21 tests "error mapping" — untestable without one), and `$defs`-hosted ArtifactReference/ActorIdentity/ExternalReference. Replace WorkContract's `authority` object with a reference to the policy type rather than an inline 4-key subset.

findings.claim: The digest chain that makes the protocol tamper-evident is broken in three places: no canonical-JSON or hash algorithm is specified anywhere, ExecutionReceipt has no digest field despite 05 mandating one, and VerificationVerdict references its EvidenceBundle by bare ID with no digest — so a verdict can be silently re-pointed at different bundle content.
findings.evidence: 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:25 — "canonical JSON используется для digest/signature" is the ONLY mention; `rg 'sha256|SHA-256|JCS|RFC 8785|digest algorithm'` across the whole pack returns only FPV-02.md:32 ("Canonical JSON serialization and digest algorithm" as future scope). 05-EXECUTION-RECEIPT.md:32 requires "receipt digest"; `rg digest protocol/schemas/execution-receipt.schema.json` returns only lines 36 and 45 — both inside the nested `contract` object — and `additionalProperties: false` (line 6) blocks adding one: empirical `receipt with digest (per 05 line 32): ["Additional properties are not allowed ('digest' was unexpected)"]`. verification-verdict.schema.json:34-35 declares `"evidence_bundle": {"type": "string"}` with no digest companion, while evidence-bundle.schema.json:30-48 does bind its contract by `{id, version, digest}`. Consequence: 16-CONFORMANCE.md:29 compares "contract digest" across Cursor/Codex/OpenCode — not reproducible without a named canonicalization.
findings.recommendation: Name the algorithm normatively in 03 (e.g. RFC 8785 JCS + SHA-256, lowercase hex, digest computed over the document with the `digest` field omitted) and constrain every `digest` field with a matching `pattern`. Add a top-level `digest` to ExecutionReceipt. Change `verification-verdict.evidence_bundle` from a string to `{id, digest}` and add a `repository: {base_sha, result_sha}` binding so the `stale` verdict required by 06:56 ("изменённый base SHA требует revalidation") is derivable from the verdict document itself.

findings.claim: The same conceptual field has different types in different schemas: `contract` is an object `{id, version, digest}` in ExecutionReceipt and EvidenceBundle but a bare string in VerificationVerdict. There is zero shared-type reuse — no `$defs`, no `$ref` anywhere in any of the 5 schemas.
findings.evidence: execution-receipt.schema.json:31-50 and evidence-bundle.schema.json:30-48 both define `"contract": {"type": "object", "required": ["id","version","digest"]}` (duplicated, not shared). verification-verdict.schema.json:31-33 defines `"contract": {"type": "string"}`. Python scan across all 5 files: `contains $ref: False | contains $defs: False` for every schema. ArtifactReference is likewise inlined ad hoc at work-contract.schema.json:50-68 and reused nowhere.
findings.recommendation: Introduce a shared `$defs` bundle (or a `common.v1.json` with `$ref`) hosting ContractRef, ArtifactReference, ActorIdentity, Digest and ExternalReference, and make VerificationVerdict.contract a ContractRef. Without this, a verdict cannot be checked against the contract version it judged, and every adapter will re-derive an incompatible shape.

findings.claim: The protocol conflicts with this repo's shipped evidence model: `congruence` is required by the pack's own R_eff formula but has no field in EvidenceBundle, and the new fourth verdict value `unknown` is silently coerced to `Supports` by the existing parser — a trust-inflation path, not a compatible extension.
findings.evidence: 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:65 — `claim_score = evaluate(supports, weakens, refutes, congruence, freshness, provenance)`; evidence-bundle.schema.json:111-129 defines an evidence item as only `{kind, verdict, provenance, artifact_ref}` — no congruence, no freshness, no evidence_type. CLAUDE.md mandates `verdict/congruence_level/evidence_type` in every EvidencePack; 145 of 148 files in .forgeplan/evidence/ carry `congruence_level` and `evidence_type` (counted). crates/forgeplan-core/src/scoring/reff.rs:20-24 defines `enum Verdict { Supports, Weakens, Refutes }` — only 3 variants; crates/forgeplan-core/src/scoring/evidence.rs:59-65 maps any unrecognised string via `_ => Verdict::Supports`, so a protocol bundle carrying `verdict: "unknown"` (evidence-bundle.schema.json:116-121) scores 1.0 instead of being rejected. Note the same file fails CLOSED to CL0 for garbage `congruence_level` (evidence.rs:76-88) — the existing code is strictly more conservative than the new protocol.
findings.recommendation: Add `congruence_level` (0-3 integer) and `evidence_type` (enum measurement/test/benchmark/audit) to the evidence item so the wire format can express what R_eff consumes and what 145 existing artifacts already carry. Either drop `unknown` from the verdict enum or, before introducing it, change reff.rs `Verdict` to a 4th fail-closed variant scoring 0.0 — the current `_ => Supports` fallback makes `unknown` a silent upgrade. FPV-06 should list this coercion explicitly as migration scope; it currently does not.

findings.claim: `provenance` — the field the entire "verify the artifact, not the claim" premise rests on — is declared as an unconstrained `{"type": "object"}`, and `kind` is a free string with no controlled vocabulary shared with the contract's `evidence_required[].kinds`, so the Verification Engine has nothing to match on.
findings.evidence: evidence-bundle.schema.json:123-125 — `"provenance": {"type": "object"}` (no required keys); 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:26 lists "Evidence artifact hashes" as mandatory data, and 06:33 step 3 is "проверить provenance" — neither is expressible in a checkable way. `"kind": {"type": "string"}` (line 112-114) vs work-contract.schema.json:203-209 `"kinds": {"items": {"type": "string"}}` — two free-text lists that the engine must reconcile. Empirical: `kind: "vibes"` with `provenance: {}` validates with 0 errors.
findings.recommendation: Define an `EvidenceKind` enum shared by both documents (test_report, build_log, benchmark, ci_run, security_scan, ui_capture, audit, measurement) and give `provenance` required structure: `{source, hash, algorithm, collected_at, collector_actor}`. Until `provenance` has required fields, 06's gate "test claim без отчёта/CI receipt не проходит" (06:57) is a prose promise with no wire representation.

findings.claim: WorkContract is missing two of its own declared mandatory sections (external execution constraints; escalation and rollback rules), makes `constraints` optional despite listing it as mandatory, and has no representation at all for the contract provenance the compiler is required to emit.
findings.evidence: 04-WORK-CONTRACT.md:9-22 "Обязательные разделы" includes "applicable constraints and decisions", "external execution constraints", "escalation and rollback rules". work-contract.schema.json:7-20 `required` omits `constraints`; there is no `external_execution`, no `escalation`, no `rollback` property, and `additionalProperties: false` (line 6) forbids adding them. 04:46-55 requires per-derived-element provenance `{source_artifact, source_section/field, source_digest, compiler_rule}`; compiler duty #9 (04:43) is "объяснить происхождение каждого contract field" and acceptance criterion 04:72 is "source provenance доступен для каждого derived field" — the schema offers only `constraints[].source` as a bare string (line 160-162) and nothing at all on `acceptance[]` (lines 170-189). FPV-03 (deterministic compiler) cannot meet its acceptance criteria against this schema.
findings.recommendation: Either add the three missing sections plus a `provenance` sidecar (a `provenance: {field_path -> {source_artifact, source_section, source_digest, compiler_rule}}` map, or per-element `source_ref` objects), or amend 04 to demote them from "обязательные разделы". Do not leave the doc and the schema disagreeing — FPV-03 will implement whichever it reads first.

findings.claim: ExecutionReceipt and EvidenceBundle each omit several fields their own spec sections list as mandatory, and `additionalProperties: false` makes them unrepresentable — including the `trace_id` that 03 says every operation carries and the `version` that 03 says every actor carries.
findings.evidence: 05-EXECUTION-RECEIPT.md:22-33 requires "usage/cost references" and "raw provider payload reference" — neither exists in execution-receipt.schema.json:17-143. 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:61-67 defines actor identity as `actor_id, actor_type, provider, instance_id, version`; the schema's actor object (lines 51-72) omits `version`: empirical `receipt with actor.version (per 03-PROTOCOL): ["Additional properties are not allowed ('version' was unexpected)"]`. 03:73-82 "Все операции используют: trace_id, idempotency_key, …" and 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:65 requires trace ID on every audit event — `rg trace_id` across the entire pack returns exactly one hit, 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:76, and zero schema occurrences. 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:22-24 requires "environment metadata" and "CI and PR references" — absent from evidence-bundle.schema.json; `commands` (line 137) is optional though 06:21 lists "commands with exit codes" as mandatory data.
findings.recommendation: Add `trace_id` to all four operational documents, `version` to the actor object, `usage`/`raw_payload_ref` to the receipt, and `environment` + `ci_refs`/`pr_refs` to the bundle; move `commands` into `required`. These are cheap now and expensive after FPV-04/FPV-05 land Rust DTOs against the current shapes.

findings.claim: VerificationVerdict cannot express the claim-centric R_eff it is supposed to carry: there is no required-vs-informational flag and no numeric score on criteria, so `R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)` is not reconstructible or auditable from the verdict document.
findings.evidence: 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:62-69 defines `claim_score = evaluate(...)`, `R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)` and "Informational claims не обрушивают весь decision score". work-contract.schema.json:183-186 does carry `acceptance[].required` (boolean, default true) — but verification-verdict.schema.json:47-77 gives each criterion only `{id, verdict(enum), reasons[]}`: no `required`, no `score`, no `congruence`, no evidence back-reference. There is no top-level `r_eff` either (top-level props: contract, criteria, decided_at, decided_by, digest, evidence_bundle, extensions, policy_version, protocol_version, schema, verdict, verdict_id). Also `criteria` has no `minItems`, so a verdict deciding zero criteria validates.
findings.recommendation: Add `required: boolean`, `score: number` and `evidence_refs: []` to `verification-verdict.criteria[]`, plus a top-level `r_eff` with the min-computation documented, and `minItems: 1` on `criteria`. Otherwise FPV-06's acceptance criterion "Per-source F/G/R and contribution are available in JSON" has no protocol carrier and Web v2 (FPV-14) will have to recompute scores client-side from a different source than the verdict.

findings.claim: extension-manifest cannot support Invariant 9 ("an extension cannot obtain more authority than its manifest declares"): `permissions`, `compatibility` and `conformance` are required-but-untyped `{"type": "object"}`, the manifest carries no `protocol_version` (the only one of the five schemas that does not), and its capability enum cannot express two of 07's five enforcement levels.
findings.evidence: extension-manifest.schema.json:40-42 `"compatibility": {"type": "object"}`, :55-57 `"permissions": {"type": "object"}`, :80-82 `"conformance": {"type": "object"}` — all three carry zero structure, and `compatibility`/`permissions` are in `required` (lines 12-14). 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:111 — "Extension не может получить больше полномочий, чем объявлено в manifest." Top-level props are `[capabilities, compatibility, conformance, id, kind, maturity, ownership, permissions, schema, version]` — no `protocol_version`, unlike the other four schemas which all require it. Enum conflict: 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:55-59 defines enforcement levels {full, core, ci, advisory, unsupported} and 07:61 states "Capability matrix обязана показывать реальный уровень", but extension-manifest.schema.json:45-53 and 16-CONFORMANCE.md:43-47 use {full, partial, advisory, unsupported, experimental} — `core` and `ci` have no home in any schema.
findings.recommendation: Add `protocol_version` to the manifest. Give `permissions` a closed shape keyed by the 13 actions from 07 with an explicit grant list, and `compatibility` a `{protocol: "^1.", forgeplan: semver-range}` shape. Resolve the two 5-value level enums: they are different axes (what a host CAN enforce vs WHERE enforcement happens) and should be two separate named fields, not one overloaded word.

findings.claim: The Deep/Critical separation-of-duties rule is undecidable from the protocol: `producer`, `verifier` and `decided_by` are bare strings rather than ActorIdentity, so "different actor instances" cannot be evaluated because `instance_id` is not carried.
findings.evidence: 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:47 — "Builder и verifier обязаны быть разными actor instances"; 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:108 — "Critical execution не может быть принято тем же actor, который его выполнял." evidence-bundle.schema.json:53-58 `"producer": {"type": "string"}`, `"verifier": {"type": "string"}`; verification-verdict.schema.json:86-87 `"decided_by": {"type": "string"}`. ExecutionReceipt does model actor structurally (execution-receipt.schema.json:51-72) — the three documents disagree on how an actor is represented.
findings.recommendation: Use one ActorIdentity `$def` in all three documents (`{actor_id, actor_type, provider, instance_id, version}`). A string cannot distinguish two instances of the same agent, so the Deep-profile gate would have to be enforced out-of-band with no auditable record in the bundle or the verdict.

findings.claim: The pack ships zero fixture instances and its own validator never validates anything against the schemas — it only checks that the files parse as JSON, so none of the defects above would be caught by running the pack's tooling.
findings.evidence: `find docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer -type f` lists 5 schema files and no examples/fixtures directory. scripts/validate_pack.py:24-25 — `for schema in (root/'protocol/schemas').glob('*.json'): json.loads(schema.read_text(...))` — no meta-schema check, no instance validation. Its success line (:26) reports "N schemas" as if they were verified. 16-CONFORMANCE.md:27 requires "Один fixture WorkContract" executed in Cursor, Codex and OpenCode, and FPV-02.md:33 lists "fixture corpus with valid/invalid examples" as scope — neither exists yet. (For the record, all 5 schemas DO pass Draft202012Validator.check_schema — verified independently with jsonschema 4.23.0.)
findings.recommendation: Add a `protocol/fixtures/{valid,invalid}/` corpus now — in particular the negative cases proven above (empty SHAs, base==result, zero criteria, unknown field round-trip) — and extend validate_pack.py to run `Draft202012Validator.check_schema` plus instance validation over the corpus. Otherwise FPV-02's AC "Rust and JSON schema validation agree on fixture corpus" has nothing to agree on.

findings.claim: The verdict vocabulary is inconsistent across the pack: the data-flow diagram advertises four outcomes with a hyphenated name that matches no schema value, while the schema and 06 define six.
findings.evidence: 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:98 — `accepted / rejected / incomplete / human-review` (4 values, `human-review`). 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:44-50 and verification-verdict.schema.json:38-45 — `accepted, rejected, incomplete, blocked, requires_human_review, stale` (6 values, `requires_human_review`). A reader implementing from the diagram would emit an invalid verdict.
findings.recommendation: Fix 02:98 to list all six with the exact schema spellings, or annotate it as an abridged illustration. Cheap, but this is the diagram most readers will copy from.

summary: The 18 docs describe a directionally coherent product boundary (intent → contract → evidence → verdict) and are unusually disciplined about what ForgePlan must NOT become. But they are a positioning document wearing an architecture document's clothes: the three mechanisms the entire program rests on — unforgeable actor identity, persistence of the new protocol objects, and independent recomputation of the git delta — are never specified, and the separation-of-duties invariants (02:106, 02:108) are therefore unenforceable as written. The pack also silently reverses an active ADR (ADR-001 "No adapter traits", status: active) with no supersede path, creates zero artifacts in `.forgeplan/` for a 3-repo/16-issue program, and contains no migration story at all for 65 existing PRDs, 148 EvidencePacks or today's `R_eff = min(evidence_scores)` — `grep -rn -i "migrat|backward|legacy|существующ"` over all 18 docs returns only an extension-kind name and a docs-nav bullet. Several load-bearing claims about third-party hosts (Cursor hooks, Codex skills, OpenCode permissions, Conductor beta API) are asserted with zero citations and zero version pins, while doc 18 gates the release on those hosts passing a conformance suite that defines no pass criterion.

findings.claim: The authority model, the separation-of-duties invariants and the Critical-depth gate all depend on actor identity being unforgeable, but no doc specifies how an actor_id is authenticated or attested — an adapter self-reports it.
findings.evidence: 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:69 `actor_id является непрозрачным стабильным ID. Display name не используется как authority key.` — the only statement about identity trust. 02:108 `6. Critical execution не может быть принято тем же actor, который его выполнял.` 07:47 `Builder и verifier обязаны быть разными actor instances.` The only crypto in the pack is 03:100 `contracts и verdicts получают digest;` and 03:25 `canonical JSON используется для digest/signature` — a digest proves content integrity, not who produced it, and no key issuance, signing authority or attestation is defined anywhere (`grep -rn 'http' architecture/` returns nothing; no key-management section exists).
findings.recommendation: Before FPV-07 (Authority) is scheduled, add a decision (as an ADR in .forgeplan/adrs/) defining actor credentialing: who issues actor_id, what binds a submission to it (signature over the canonical EvidenceBundle digest, CI OIDC token, host-attested identity), and what core does when identity is unattested. Until then, downgrade invariants 6 and 07's Deep/Critical profiles from 'enforced' to 'advisory' in the docs so they are not advertised as guarantees.

findings.claim: No doc decides where WorkContracts, ExecutionReceipts, EvidenceBundles, Verdicts and the append-only authority log are persisted — which collides head-on with ADR-003 (markdown = source of truth) and RED LINE #11 (artifacts mutated only via MCP/CLI).
findings.evidence: 05:18 `ForgePlan хранит нормализованную receipt и external references.` 11:27 `ForgePlan хранит contract, receipt, Evidence и verdict.` 03:102 `Evidence artifacts могут храниться снаружи, но hash и metadata сохраняются в ForgePlan;` 07:65 `Authority decisions append-only…`. `grep -rn -i 'storage|persist|\.forgeplan|markdown|lance' architecture/` returns exactly those four lines and 14:46 (`storage/search implementation details` — listed as something to REMOVE from the site). Meanwhile .forgeplan/adrs/ADR-003-…md:8 `status: active`, title `Markdown files as source of truth — LanceDB as index layer`, and CLAUDE.md:174 `| Решения | .forgeplan/adrs/ | ADR — единственное место`.
findings.recommendation: Add a persistence doc (or a section in 02) deciding, per protocol object: git-tracked markdown/JSON under .forgeplan/, gitignored derived index, or external store. High-frequency machine-written objects (receipts, verdicts, audit events) must NOT land in the git-tracked artifact tree without an explicit ADR-003 amendment — otherwise every agent execution mutates the repo's source of truth and RED LINE #11 becomes unenforceable.

findings.claim: Verification is defined as ground-truth git-delta checking, but the delta is provider-reported and the pack forbids ForgePlan from owning the workspace — so no doc explains how core obtains the objects needed to recompute it.
findings.evidence: 05:30 `- changed paths reported by provider;` versus 06:3 `> Verify the artifact, not the claim.` and 06:56 `changed paths вне allowed scope блокируют acceptance;`. 06:16-18 puts `base SHA and result SHA; changed paths and git delta digest` in the bundle — i.e. also supplied by the producer. 01:38 lists `worktree manager` under `ForgePlan не является`, and 11:23 says Conductor owns the workspace, 10:17 `Cursor владеет worktree, sandbox и session.` Nothing in 06 says core recomputes `git diff base..result` itself, and nothing says how a cloud-host result SHA becomes fetchable locally.
findings.recommendation: State explicitly in 06 that core recomputes changed_paths and delta_digest from git objects and treats provider-reported paths as untrusted hints; then add the missing precondition — how the result revision is made reachable (adapter must push the branch / provide a bundle / supply a signed CI attestation) and what verdict is emitted when it is not (`incomplete`, not `accepted`).

findings.claim: The pack reverses an active ADR (ADR-001 'No adapter traits — AI agent is the orchestrator, not Forgeplan') without naming it, superseding it, or creating any ForgePlan artifact for the program.
findings.evidence: .forgeplan/adrs/ADR-001-…md:10 `status: active`; :30 `**Отвергаем adapter traits.** Forgeplan НЕ интегрируется напрямую с внешними системами (кроме LLM).`; :32 `Интеграция — ответственность AI agent (Claude Code)`. Against that, 09:52-61 `Core предоставляет стабильные ports:` ContractReader / ExecutionRegistrar / EvidenceSubmitter / VerdictReader / PolicyEvaluator / ExternalReferenceStore, and 11:15-27 defines direct Kandev/Vibe/Conductor/Paperclip adapters. `grep -rli 'vnext|workcontract|executionreceipt' .forgeplan` returns nothing — the whole program has zero artifacts in the graph, while the pack's own rule AGENTS-VNEXT.md:12 demands `Создать или обновить нужный PRD/RFC/ADR/Spec до code changes` and CLAUDE.md:174 makes .forgeplan/adrs the only home for decisions.
findings.recommendation: Before FPV-01 merges: create the vNext EPIC + PRD + a boundary ADR via MCP/CLI, and explicitly supersede ADR-001 (`forgeplan supersede ADR-001 --by <new>`), documenting why the 'agent is the orchestrator' decision no longer holds. Docs 09/11 should cite the superseding ADR rather than silently contradicting an active one.

findings.claim: Zero migration or backward-compatibility content across all 18 docs: nothing decides what happens to 65 existing PRDs, 148 EvidencePacks, today's R_eff, or already-activated artifacts when claim-centric scoring lands.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn -i 'migrat|backward|back-compat|обратн|legacy|существующ' architecture/` yields only 09:10 `- migration_pack;`, 02:62 `- migration packs.`, 12:15 `Migration Packs`, 15:13 `9. Operations — … migration.` — none of which define one. 06:62-67 replaces the shipped `R_eff = min(evidence_scores)` (CLAUDE.md:682; crates/forgeplan-core/src/scoring/reff.rs:75) with `R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)` while the repo holds `ls .forgeplan/prds | wc -l` = 65, `ls .forgeplan/evidence | wc -l` = 148. 18-RELEASE-CRITERIA.md contains no migration criterion at all. Even the issue defers it: issues/forgeplan/FPV-06.md:41 `Document whether R_eff v2 is opt-in, schema-version gated or introduced by major version.`
findings.recommendation: Add a migration section to 06 and a release criterion to 18 answering: do existing EvidencePacks (verdict/congruence_level/evidence_type) map to claims automatically or become 'informational'; do already-activated artifacts get re-scored and can activation be revoked; is R_eff v2 opt-in behind a config flag for one minor release. Ship a dry-run command that prints old-vs-new scores for the existing 65 PRDs before the switch.

findings.claim: The ownership matrix violates the pack's own 'One owner per state' principle in its own table: workspace/worktree/session is assigned to two owners with 'or', and 10/11 then have Cursor and Conductor/Vibe each claiming it with no precedence rule.
findings.evidence: 01:52 `| Workspace, worktree, branch, session | Agent host или orchestrator |` directly against 01:85 `**O — One owner per state.** Для каждого состояния существует один источник истины.` Then 10:17 `Cursor владеет worktree, sandbox и session.` and 11:19 `Vibe Kanban владеет issue, workspace/worktree, agent session…`, 11:23 `Conductor владеет workspace, session, harness, terminal, diff и PR.` The realistic stack (Conductor driving Cursor) has two declared owners of the same state and no arbitration rule; 11:34 only forbids ForgePlan from creating worktrees.
findings.recommendation: Replace the 'or' with a precedence rule: when an orchestrator adapter is present it owns workspace/session and the host adapter is a nested executor; the ExecutionReceipt must record which layer is authoritative (a single `owner` field) so external references cannot be double-claimed. Add a conformance check for the both-present case.

findings.claim: The semantic-portability test is unsatisfiable by construction: it compares changed-path sets and final verdicts across hosts whose enforcement levels are, by the pack's own model, allowed to differ from 'full' to 'advisory'.
findings.evidence: 16:27 `Один fixture WorkContract выполняется минимум в Cursor, Codex и OpenCode.` and 16:29-34 compares `allowed/forbidden behavior; changed path set; … final VerificationVerdict.` But 07:55-59 defines `full — host adapter технически блокирует нарушение` … `advisory — только предупреждение` … `unsupported — host не может обеспечить правило`, and 10:57 states the generic/portable integration ships `advisory policy when hooks unavailable`. A contract that exercises a forbidden path yields a blocked edit under `full` and a completed edit under `advisory` — different changed-path sets and different verdicts, by design. 16 also never defines what 'passing' means per capability level, yet 18:27 makes `Cursor, Codex и OpenCode прошли Host Conformance v1` a release gate.
findings.recommendation: Split the suite: (a) semantic parity of contract digest + required Evidence + criterion verdicts given the SAME observed delta (must be identical everywhere); (b) enforcement-behaviour tests scored per declared capability level, where 'pass' means the observed behaviour matches the manifest's declared level. Define pass/fail explicitly in 16 before 18:27 can be evaluated.

findings.claim: Web v2 (Phase 5) requires execution/evidence data that only the optional server (Phase 6) is chartered to ingest — a sequencing inversion the roadmap does not resolve, and doc 13 never names a data source.
findings.evidence: 13:25-31 Execution view requires `host/orchestrator; external task/workspace/session IDs; actor; base/result SHA; changed paths; PR/CI links` and 13:34-35 a `Verification timeline`. 17:46-52 places `ForgePlan Web v2` in Phase 5; 17:54-61 places `remote MCP/server; event ingestion; auth and audit` in Phase 6 — and 02:70 says the server is the `Поздний опциональный слой для remote MCP, event ingestion`. Doc 13 contains no statement of where Web reads from (no storage/API section anywhere in the file).
findings.recommendation: Either (a) declare Web v2 scope as repo-local read of git-tracked protocol objects (which forces finding VNEXT-ARCH-02 to be decided first), or (b) move the minimal ingestion slice from Phase 6 into Phase 5 as a hard dependency. Add a 'Data sources' section to 13 naming exactly which files/endpoints each view reads.

findings.claim: The core scoring function of the whole program is an undefined placeholder, and four other load-bearing gates are stated in terms that cannot be implemented or falsified as written.
findings.evidence: 06:65 `claim_score = evaluate(supports, weakens, refutes, congruence, freshness, provenance)` — the replacement for the shipped R_eff is a function name with no formula, no weights, no ranges. 06:54 `code-claiming Evidence с пустым relevant delta не проходит` — 'relevant' is never defined (no criterion→path mapping exists). 04:38 `найти active decisions, которые применимы к affected paths/domain` — 'применимы' and 'domain' undefined. 04:44 `отказать при unresolved contradictions` — no contradiction detector is specified. 04:61 `repair execution может использовать тот же contract, если intent не изменился` — unfalsifiable. 07:39 `…разрешены при полном deterministic verification` — 'полное' undefined.
findings.recommendation: For each: give a computable definition or mark it explicitly as an open decision blocking the dependent issue. `evaluate()` in particular must become a written formula with a worked example and golden test vectors in FPV-06, since 06:67 `R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)` is meaningless without it.

findings.claim: The protocol's forward-compatibility rule contradicts the shipped v1 schemas: unknown optional fields must survive round-trip, but every schema sets additionalProperties:false at every level, so a 1.1 document fails 1.0 validation.
findings.evidence: 03:20-24 `patch — совместимые исправления и новые optional fields; minor — совместимые расширения semantics; … unknown optional fields должны сохраняться при round-trip;`. But work-contract.schema.json:6 `"additionalProperties": false,` (repeated at :71, :90, :106, :142, :164, :188, :211, :248), execution-receipt.schema.json:6, evidence-bundle.schema.json:6, verification-verdict.schema.json:6, extension-manifest.schema.json:6 — all closed, and `"protocol_version": {"pattern": "^1\\."}` accepts 1.1 documents that the closed schema then rejects.
findings.recommendation: Decide the compat mechanism now: either open the objects (`additionalProperties: true` plus a reserved `extensions` namespace, which already exists at work-contract.schema.json:250) or drop the round-trip-preservation promise from 03. Add a compatibility fixture — a synthetic 1.1 document that a 1.0 consumer must accept and re-emit unchanged — to FPV-02's acceptance.

findings.claim: Doc 04 declares 12 mandatory WorkContract sections and a per-field provenance requirement that the v1 schema cannot express and, being closed, cannot be extended to express.
findings.evidence: 04:21 `- external execution constraints;` and 04:22 `- escalation and rollback rules;` have no counterpart in work-contract.schema.json (required list at :7-20 is schema/protocol_version/contract_id/version/digest/source/repository/objective/scope/acceptance/evidence_required/authority; top-level `additionalProperties: false` at :6 blocks adding them). 04:43 `9. объяснить происхождение каждого contract field;` and 04:48-55 require `source_artifact / source_section / source_digest / compiler_rule` per derived element — but acceptance items carry only `id`/`claim`/`required` (:172-186) with `additionalProperties:false` (:188), and constraints carry a bare `source` string (:160). 04:72 makes `source provenance доступен для каждого derived field` an acceptance condition that the schema makes unrepresentable.
findings.recommendation: Reconcile 04 and the schema in the same PR (FPV-02/FPV-03): add `provenance` objects to acceptance/constraint/evidence_required items and top-level `escalation`/`external_execution` blocks, or delete those requirements from 04. A design pack whose spec and schema disagree on required content will burn a full review cycle at implementation time.

findings.claim: Invariant 7 forbids duplicating external runtime state, yet doc 05 defines a nine-state normalized status mirror with no owner, no update mechanism and no staleness rule.
findings.evidence: 02:109 `7. External task/runtime state не дублируется в ForgePlan.` versus 05:28 `- normalized status;` and 05:37-47 `registered / running / blocked / awaiting_review / completed / failed / cancelled / expired / superseded`. 05:55 tries to defuse it — `external status не становится вторым каноническим task state в ForgePlan` — but a mirrored `running`/`blocked` field IS duplicated runtime state; nothing says who writes transitions (adapter push? core poll?), what TTL applies, or what a receipt stuck in `running` means.
findings.recommendation: Either reduce the receipt to terminal-only states (registered → {completed|failed|cancelled} plus an opaque `external_status` string that core never interprets), or keep the nine states and add an ownership/refresh rule: who writes each transition, expiry semantics for `running`, and what verification does with a stale receipt.

findings.claim: 'Not a scheduler' is asserted as canonical while core keeps claims/leases and the shipped forgeplan dispatch — a conflict the pack's own issue admits is undecided.
findings.evidence: 01:39 lists `- scheduler;` under `ForgePlan не является`, and the ownership matrix (01:48-58) never mentions dispatch or claims. 02:46 keeps `- claims/leases;` inside ForgePlan Core. The shipped product has `forgeplan dispatch --agents N` / `claim` / `release` (CLAUDE.md multi-agent section). issues/forgeplan/FPV-01.md:21 concedes the decision is open: `Decide whether current dispatch scheduling remains core, becomes an optional planner adapter, or is retained only as advisory graph analysis.`

findings.claim: Verdict vocabulary and Evidence obligations drift between docs and schemas: 02's flow omits two verdicts and renames one, and the EvidenceBundle schema demands a git delta for every bundle while invariant 5 restricts that to code-claiming Evidence.
findings.evidence: 02:98 ` accepted / rejected / incomplete / human-review` versus 06:43-50 `accepted / rejected / incomplete / blocked / requires_human_review / stale` and verification-verdict.schema.json:38-45 (six values, `requires_human_review`). 02:107 `5. Для code-claiming Evidence обязательны base SHA и result SHA.` versus evidence-bundle.schema.json:14 (`repository` in the top-level required list) and :61-66 requiring `base_sha, result_sha, changed_paths, delta_digest` unconditionally — so a benchmark-only or design-review bundle is unrepresentable.
findings.recommendation: Make 02:98 quote the canonical six verdicts, and make the EvidenceBundle `repository` block conditionally required (JSON Schema `if/then` on the presence of a code-claiming criterion) so non-code Evidence remains expressible.

findings.claim: Every third-party capability claim on which the adapter and conformance programs depend is asserted with no citation and no supported-version pin, while three docs require version matrices.
findings.evidence: `grep -rn 'http' architecture/` returns nothing — zero references in 1171 lines. 10:11 asserts Cursor supports `pre-tool, post-tool и stop hooks`; 10:21-22 asserts a Codex `.agents/skills/forge/` convention; 10:44 `OpenCode рекомендуется как reference adapter для granular permissions` with no supporting data; 11:23 `Adapter должен быть versioned из-за beta API` is the ONLY version-related statement in either doc (`grep -inE 'version|v[0-9]' 10 11` returns just that line). Yet 09:37 requires manifests to declare `supported host versions`, 12:26 `host/orchestrator versions`, and 18:51 `version matrix generated from conformance`.

Host adapter issues (FPV-12/13) should not start until each target's enforcement primitives are confirmed to exist — the whole 'full vs advisory' model depends on it.

findings.claim: Mid-execution scope expansion — the single most common real-world event — is never specified, despite being an explicit authority action and a declared invariant.
findings.evidence: 02:103-105 `WorkContract immutable после начала исполнения. Scope expansion создаёт новую версию контракта. Исполнитель не может изменить acceptance criteria запущенного контракта.` 07:26 lists action `contract.expand_scope;` and work-contract.schema.json:229 has `authority.expand_scope`. But 04:58-63 only says `после запуска scope/criteria/policy не меняются` and `change request создаёт новую contract version` — nothing states what happens to the in-flight ExecutionReceipt (which binds contract id+version+digest, execution-receipt.schema.json:31-48), whether it becomes `superseded` (a status that exists at 05:46 but is never explained), whether partial Evidence carries over, or who pauses the agent.
findings.recommendation: Add a 'Scope expansion during execution' section to 04 or 05: contract vN+1 is compiled, the in-flight receipt transitions to `superseded`, a new execution is registered against vN+1, and Evidence collected under vN is admissible only for criteria whose IDs and digests are unchanged.

findings.claim: The 'no static counts' rule collides with an existing CI gate and with the repo's own documentation practice; no doc says what replaces the gate.
findings.evidence: 12:48 `README и сайт генерируются из manifests. Static counts запрещены.` and 15:46 `counts не хранятся вручную.` and 14:41 removes `количество MCP tools и CLI commands` from the first screen. Against that, CLAUDE.md:447 documents an active CI drift detector `scripts/check-mcp-tool-count.sh` (present, executable) whose entire purpose is to keep manually written doc counts in sync with code, and CLAUDE.md:100 itself carries `**76 CLI commands**, **73 MCP tools**`.

findings.claim: The optional Server — the component that would resolve the identity and persistence blockers — has three lines of architecture in the entire pack, yet carries auth, audit, multi-repo registry and OTel in Phase 6.
findings.evidence: 02:68-70 is the complete specification: `Поздний опциональный слой для remote MCP, event ingestion, auth, audit и multi-repository registry. Не запускает агентов и не заменяет orchestrators.` 17:54-61 then assigns it `remote MCP/server; event ingestion; auth and audit; OpenTelemetry; multi-repo registry; replay and idempotency.` There is no 19-SERVER doc — `ls architecture/` ends at 18-RELEASE-CRITERIA.md — while every other component (Web, Marketplace, adapters) has a dedicated file.
findings.recommendation: Either write the server doc (even three pages: trust model, what it stores, what it never stores, degradation to local-only) or delete it from 17 until Phases 1-5 are done. Leaving auth/audit in an unspecified optional component is what makes findings 01 and 02 look deferrable when they are not.

area: Governance and prompt layer vs CLAUDE.md (ForgePlan vNext engineering-contract-layer pack)
summary: The pack's governance layer is internally coherent but is written as if this repository had no methodology of its own: across all of `governance/`, `prompts/`, `issues/` and `README.md` there are zero references to `CLAUDE.md`, zero references to any `forgeplan_*` MCP/CLI mutation tool, zero references to `cargo`/`fmt`/`clippy`, zero references to the `dev` base branch, and zero references to `## Structured Fields`. The result is not stylistic drift — it is a set of instructions that, followed literally, produce PRs targeting `main`, Evidence that scores CL0/R_eff≈0, `.forgeplan/` artifacts mutated by direct file edits (RED LINE #11), and PRs opened before the audit/test/fmt/lint gate and without user approval (RED LINES #2 and #5). Two mechanisms the pack relies on are inert as shipped: the new PR template sits in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` with no default template, so GitHub never applies it; and "independent verification" has no enforcement — the `dev` ruleset requires `required_approving_review_count: 0` and there is no CODEOWNERS. One instructed command, `forgeplan context`, exists but errors when invoked as the pack instructs. Issue bodies are correctly English (verified: 0 Cyrillic characters across all 16), which is the one language-rule item the pack gets right.

findings.claim: The pack's Evidence definition omits the `## Structured Fields` block (verdict / congruence_level / evidence_type), so every EvidencePack produced by a pack-following agent silently parses as CL0 and scores R_eff ≈ 0 — and ISSUE-GOVERNANCE additionally permits closing an issue on an "equivalent receipt" instead of an Evidence artifact.
findings.evidence: AGENTS-VNEXT.md:18 — "10. Создать Evidence с точными командами, exit codes, base/result SHA и changed paths." ISSUE-BUILDER.md:15 — "11. Создай Evidence с base SHA, result SHA, changed paths, командами, exit codes и результатами." ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:41 — "- Evidence artifact or equivalent receipt linked;". Grep over the whole pack for the required fields returns only prose hits, never the contract: `grep -rn "Structured Fields\|congruence\|verdict:" .` → architecture/06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:36, issues/bodies.json:35 (FPV-06 AC), issues/forgeplan/FPV-06.md:24, prompts/INDEPENDENT-VERIFIER.md:14 — no instruction anywhere to emit the three fields. CLAUDE.md:16 (RED LINE #7) — "**EvidencePack body MUST contain** `verdict:`, `congruence_level:`, `evidence_type:` — без этих structured fields parser тихо ставит CL0 (silent failure → R_eff = 0.1)."
findings.recommendation: Add to AGENTS-VNEXT.md and ISSUE-BUILDER.md an explicit Evidence body contract: the EvidencePack MUST contain a `## Structured Fields` section with `verdict:`, `congruence_level:`, `evidence_type:` in addition to SHAs/commands/exit codes. Delete "or equivalent receipt" from ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:41 or define precisely which receipt satisfies R_eff scoring — an unscored receipt cannot close an issue in this repo.

findings.claim: The pack instructs agents to create and update PRD/RFC/ADR/Spec artifacts but never names the mandated mutation channel, so an agent following it will edit `.forgeplan/**/*.md` directly — the exact action RED LINE #11 forbids, which desynchronizes LanceDB, the state machine and the canonical body.
findings.evidence: AGENTS-VNEXT.md:12 — "4. Создать или обновить нужный PRD/RFC/ADR/Spec до code changes." (no channel specified). `grep -rnE "forgeplan_(new|update|link|activate)|mcp__forgeplan" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches. `grep -rn "\.forgeplan" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → exactly one hit, prompts/ISSUE-BUILDER.md:8 "Найди связанные `.forgeplan/` artifacts" (read-only). CLAUDE.md:20 (RED LINE #11) — "файлы в `.forgeplan/{prds,adrs,specs,rfcs,evidence,notes}/*.md` нельзя редактировать через `Edit`/`Write`/`sed` напрямую."
findings.recommendation: Insert a hard boundary in AGENTS-VNEXT.md and ISSUE-BUILDER.md: all artifact creation/mutation goes through `mcp__forgeplan__forgeplan_new|forgeplan_update|forgeplan_link|forgeplan_activate` (or the CLI equivalents), never `Edit`/`Write`/`sed`, plus the recovery path (`forgeplan_update id=<ID> body=<full body>`, last-resort `forgeplan scan-import`).

findings.claim: The pack directs agents to branch and open PRs autonomously and never names a base branch; `origin/HEAD` points at `main`, so `gh pr create` defaults to `main` — violating both the dev-based branching model and RED LINE #2 (no push until the user explicitly approves after review).
findings.evidence: PROGRAM-COORDINATOR.md:24 — "9. Создай отдельную bootstrap-ветку, закоммить только пакет документации/автоматизации и открой draft PR в `ForgePlan/forgeplan`." ISSUE-BUILDER.md:16 — "12. Открой draft PR, свяжи issue…". AGENTS-VNEXT.md:14 — "6. Создать отдельную branch/worktree через текущий orchestrator." `grep -rniE "\bdev\b|--base" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → only `https://forgeplan.dev/schemas/...` `$id` URLs in protocol/schemas/*.json; no base-branch instruction exists. `git symbolic-ref refs/remotes/origin/HEAD` → `refs/remotes/origin/main`. CLAUDE.md:11 (RED LINE #2) — "**DO NOT `git push`** until the user has explicitly approved the PR after review." CLAUDE.md:385 — "**Branching (dev-based)**: `main` ← `release/v0.x.0` ← `dev` ← `feat/*`, `fix/*`, `docs/*`."
findings.recommendation: State the base branch explicitly everywhere a PR is opened (`gh pr create --base dev`; only `release/v*` targets `main`), and add a human-approval gate before any `git push`/`gh pr create` in both PROGRAM-COORDINATOR.md and ISSUE-BUILDER.md. Without this the very first coordinator run pushes a bootstrap PR at `main` unattended.

findings.claim: The pack inverts the mandated pre-PR pipeline — the draft PR is opened first and the verifier runs after — and contains no Rust quality gate at all (no cargo fmt/check/test/clippy), so RED LINE #5 (Code → Audit → Fix → Test → Fmt → Lint → Verify before PR) cannot be satisfied by following the pack.
findings.evidence: ISSUE-BUILDER.md:16 — "12. Открой draft PR, свяжи issue и передай отдельному verifier-агенту." (verification is step 12+, after the PR). AGENTS-VNEXT.md:17-20 — "9. Запустить все команды проверки из issue. 10. Создать Evidence… 11. Отдельный verifier должен проверить PR… 12. PR должен ссылаться на issue…". `grep -rn "cargo" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches; `grep -rniE "clippy|cargo fmt" …` → 0 matches. CLAUDE.md:14 (RED LINE #5) and CLAUDE.md Rust rules #3 — "`cargo fmt` … `cargo check` — 0 warnings … `cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`".
findings.recommendation: Add a mandatory pre-PR gate step to AGENTS-VNEXT.md/ISSUE-BUILDER.md listing `cargo fmt && cargo fmt --check && cargo check && cargo test && cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets -- -D warnings`, plus the adversarial audit, and move the verifier hand-off to BEFORE `gh pr create` (or make the draft PR explicitly non-reviewable until the gate is green).

findings.claim: AGENTS-VNEXT step 3 and ISSUE-BUILDER step 5 instruct agents to run `forgeplan context` with no argument; the command exists but requires a positional `<ID>` and errors out, so the mandatory context check will always fail and be silently skipped.
findings.evidence:
AGENTS-VNEXT.md:11 — "3. Выполнить `forgeplan health`, `forgeplan context` и routing/depth check." ISSUE-BUILDER.md:9 — "5. Выполни ForgePlan health/context/depth checks." Command output: `$ forgeplan context` → "error: the following required arguments were not provided:
  <ID>

Usage: forgeplan context <ID>". Source: crates/forgeplan-cli/src/main.rs:409-412 — `Context { /// Artifact ID  id: String, … }` (non-optional positional); crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/context.rs:18 — `pub async fn run(id: &str, json: bool)`.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite the step as a concrete, runnable sequence — e.g. `forgeplan health`, `forgeplan route "<issue title>"`, and `forgeplan context <ARTIFACT-ID> --json` only once an artifact ID exists. Per CLAUDE.md's hint protocol, instructed commands must be runnable as-is with real IDs and no placeholders.

findings.claim: The new PR template will never be applied to any PR: it is the only file in `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` and the repo has no default template, so GitHub treats it as an opt-in template selectable only via `?template=` — and the pack never mentions templates anywhere, so no agent will pass the parameter.
findings.evidence: `find . -iname "pull_request_template*"` inside the repo proper returns only `./.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE` (the new directory) — there is no `.github/pull_request_template.md`, no root-level and no `docs/` template; the other hits are vendored (`sources/*`, `website/node_modules/*`, `dev/gastown`, `ref/…/payload`). `git status --short` → `?? .github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` (newly added, previously the repo had no PR template at all). `grep -rniE "pull_request_template|PR template|шаблон" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches; `grep -rn "pr create\|--base" scripts/` inside the pack → 0 matches. Consequence: the `## Evidence` table, `## Product Boundary Check` and `## Verifier` sections at lines 21-43 are inert.
findings.recommendation: Either promote it to `.github/pull_request_template.md` (accepting that it becomes the default for every PR in the repo, which needs a decision because it is much heavier than the current no-template flow), or keep the directory and document the exact invocation in AGENTS-VNEXT.md/ISSUE-BUILDER.md — `gh pr create --template forgeplan-vnext.md` / `?template=forgeplan-vnext.md` — and make the verifier reject PRs whose body lacks the required sections.

findings.claim: "Independent verification" is an honour system with no enforcement point: the `dev` ruleset requires zero approving reviews, there is no CODEOWNERS, and the only record of the verifier is a free-text line in a PR template the builder fills in itself.
findings.evidence:
`gh api repos/ForgePlan/forgeplan/rulesets/14715790` (ruleset "Dev", enforcement active) → rule `pull_request` with `{"required_approving_review_count": 0, "required_reviewers": [], "require_code_owner_review": false, "require_last_push_approval": false}`. `find . -maxdepth 3 -iname CODEOWNERS` (excluding sources/) → no result. PR template lines 39-43 — "## Verifier

- Independent verifier actor:
- Verdict:" (free text, and per GOV-06 the template is never even applied). ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:40 — "- independent verification recorded;" with no mechanism. Contrast CLAUDE.md "Adversarial audit mandate": "Each MUST find ≥3 issues. Zero findings → re-spawn (suspect superficial review)." — the pack's INDEPENDENT-VERIFIER.md:14 permits a bare `ACCEPT` with zero findings.
findings.recommendation: Bind independence to something mechanical: raise `required_approving_review_count` to 1 on the `dev` ruleset (or add CODEOWNERS), and adopt this repo's existing generator≠verifier convention — two adversarial reviewers, each required to produce ≥3 findings, zero findings triggers a re-run. Also record the verifier as a GitHub review actor, not as a self-typed line in the PR body.

findings.claim: The pack places canonical decision documents under `docs/`, which this repo forbids — decisions live only in `.forgeplan/adrs/`, and `docs/` holds guides and schemas.
findings.evidence: architecture/01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:3-11 — "## Каноническое определение … ## Главная ответственность core" (a boundary/ownership decision, not a guide). FPV-01 AC (issues/bodies.json) — "- [ ] One canonical ADR is active and linked to the vNext Epic." AND "- [ ] `docs/architecture/product-boundary.md` exists and includes ownership matrix." CLAUDE.md:174 — "| Решения | `.forgeplan/adrs/` | ADR — **единственное** место; `docs/` держит гайды и схемы, не решения |". Note the repo already has `docs/architecture/` with two files (c4-context.md, ddd-analysis-spike-3.md), so the drift predates the pack but the pack institutionalises it.
findings.recommendation: Make the ADR in `.forgeplan/adrs/` the single normative artifact for the product boundary; downgrade `docs/architecture/product-boundary.md` and `architecture/01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md` to non-normative explainers that link to the ADR, or drop the docs copy from the AC. Otherwise FPV-01 ships two competing sources of truth for the same decision on day one.

findings.claim: The repo's own pre-PR evidence hook is neutered by the pack's `FPV-NN` identifier scheme — the hook only fires when a branch or recent commit references a `PRD|RFC|ADR|EPIC|SPEC|PROB|EVID|NOTE` id, so vNext PRs will silently bypass the evidence gate.
findings.evidence: pre-pr-evidence-check.sh:122-126 — `branch_ids=$(echo "$branch" | grep -oE '(PRD|RFC|ADR|EPIC|SPEC|PROB|EVID|NOTE)-[0-9]+' …)` / `commit_ids=$(git log -20 … | grep -oE '(PRD|RFC|ADR|EPIC|SPEC|PROB|EVID|NOTE)-[0-9]+' …)`; lines 128-131 — `# No artifacts referenced → can't enforce evidence; pass.` `if [[ -z "$artifact_ids" ]]; then exit 0; fi`. `FPV-01` matches none of those prefixes. Additionally lines 114-119 bypass on `docs/*` branches, which is exactly what PROGRAM-COORDINATOR.md:24 produces ("закоммить только пакет документации/автоматизации"). The pack's PR contract (PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/forgeplan-vnext.md:3-5) asks only for `Closes: <issue URL>`, never for a `Refs: <ARTIFACT-ID>` line.
findings.recommendation: Require every vNext commit/PR to carry a `Refs: <slug or ARTIFACT-ID>` line per CLAUDE.md's commit format so the existing hook engages, and/or extend the hook's regex to recognise `FPV-\d+` mapped to its backing artifact. Track the bypass explicitly rather than letting it happen silently.

findings.claim: The pack introduces a second, competing agent rule file that no host will load and that never points back to the repository's authoritative instructions.
findings.evidence: AGENTS.md:3-9 — "This file is the **entry point**. For full details, read the files it points to. … 1. **`CLAUDE.md`** — complete project instructions … **Read this first.**" `grep -rn "CLAUDE" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches; the pack never references AGENTS.md either. AGENTS-VNEXT.md is at `docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/governance/` — a path no agent host auto-loads (hosts load root/nested `AGENTS.md`, `CLAUDE.md`), so its "Mandatory flow" (lines 7-20) reaches an agent only if a human pastes it.
findings.recommendation: Make AGENTS-VNEXT.md open with an explicit precedence clause — "CLAUDE.md and AGENTS.md are authoritative; this file adds vNext-specific rules and never overrides them" — and add a pointer to it from root AGENTS.md so it is reachable. Any pack rule that contradicts CLAUDE.md must be removed, not left for the agent to arbitrate.

findings.claim: The pack's merge discipline never states a merge method, and the `dev` ruleset permits squash — so vNext feat→dev PRs can be squash-merged, the failure mode RED LINE #4 exists to prevent.
findings.evidence: EXECUTION-ORDER.md:64-69 ("## Merge discipline") lists four rules, none about merge method; `grep -rniE "squash|merge commit" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches. `gh api repos/ForgePlan/forgeplan/rulesets/14715790` → `"allowed_merge_methods": ["merge", "squash", "rebase"]`. CLAUDE.md:388 — "feat/* → dev: **merge commit (NOT squash)** — squash loses late commits"; CLAUDE.md:13 (RED LINE #4).
findings.recommendation: Add to EXECUTION-ORDER.md "Merge discipline": feature PRs into `dev` use a merge commit, release PRs into `main` use a merge commit, squash is prohibited. Optionally tighten the `dev` ruleset's `allowed_merge_methods` to `["merge"]` so the rule is enforced rather than remembered.

findings.claim: The pack contains no language rule at all; since the agent-facing prompts are Russian and root AGENTS.md says commit bodies are "Russian preferred" while CLAUDE.md mandates English-only git/GitHub metadata, a pack-following agent will produce Russian commits and PR descriptions.
findings.location: docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/ (whole pack) vs AGENTS.md:70 vs CLAUDE.md:376-378
findings.evidence: `grep -rniE "english|английск|язык|language" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → 0 matches. AGENTS.md:70 — "**Documentation & commit bodies:** Russian preferred (matches project conventions)". CLAUDE.md:376-378 — "**🌐 Language rule (commits + PRs always EN)**: - Commit message subject and body — **English only**, no mixing. - PR title and description — **English only**." The prompts themselves are Russian (e.g. PROGRAM-COORDINATOR.md:3, ISSUE-BUILDER.md:3, INDEPENDENT-VERIFIER.md:3). Mitigating fact: the 16 GitHub issue bodies ARE compliant — a Cyrillic scan over `issues/bodies.json` reports `cyrillic_chars= 0` for every key FPV-00..FPV-15.

Separately, reconcile AGENTS.md:70 with CLAUDE.md:377 — right now the repo ships two contradictory language rules and the pack's silence lets an agent pick either.

findings.claim: Internal inconsistency in the builder/verifier severity contract: the builder is told not to accept its own "Critical" result, but "Critical" is not one of the verifier's four severity classes, so the rule maps onto nothing.
findings.evidence: ISSUE-BUILDER.md:17 — "13. Не принимай собственный Critical result и не закрывай RED-LINE findings." INDEPENDENT-VERIFIER.md:13 — "9. Классифицируй findings: RED-LINE, BLOCKER, SHOULD, COULD." AGENTS-VNEXT.md:19 uses a third phrasing — "builder не закрывает собственные RED-LINE findings" (RED-LINE only, no BLOCKER).

Also disambiguate the term RED-LINE, which currently collides with CLAUDE.md's numbered RED LINES; rename the pack's class (e.g. `VERIFIER-CRITICAL`) to avoid two meanings in one repo.

findings.claim: The coordinator prompt's step 3 depends on `scripts/install.sh`, which exists only inside the untracked `ref/` archive and was not imported into the pack — the documented bootstrap sequence is not reproducible from the repository.

Also decide whether `ref/` is tracked or gitignored — right now the only copy of the source archive is untracked and unprotected.

findings.claim: Three things the pack gets right and that should not be regressed during rework: the pack validator passes, the eight legacy issues it promises to supersede all exist and are open, and the issue bodies are already English.
