Note that `create_github_issues.py` never applies the label taxonomy from ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:5-21 — those labels are aspirational and will have to be applied by hand or added to the script.

area: ADR collision analysis — does ForgePlan vNext contradict decisions this project has already recorded?
summary: I read all 18 ADRs and the six named pack architecture documents. The pack references **zero** existing ADRs — `grep -rnoE "ADR-[0-9]{3}"` over the entire pack returns 0 hits — yet it redefines the product boundary in ways that directly contradict at least five ACTIVE ADRs (001, 003, 006, 009, 011, 015/016) and duplicates one in-flight draft (018). The single hardest blocker is that FPV-01's first acceptance criterion ("One canonical ADR is active") is unachievable as written: ADR-001 ("AI agent is the orchestrator, not Forgeplan", active) and ADR-009 ("Forgeplan as orchestrator", active) **already contradict each other today**, neither declares supersession of the other, and the pack picks a third position without naming either. Beyond that, ForgePlan already owns more workspace/agent-process state in shipped code than the pack's boundary permits (worktree resolution per ADR-015/016, `claude --print` process spawning per ADR-011), and the pack's own target architecture puts `claims/leases` inside Core while its boundary doc assigns that ownership to orchestrators. FPV-01 is **not safe to start** until the ADR-001/ADR-009 conflict is adjudicated and the pack declares which ADRs it supersedes via the ADR-005 `supersede --by` path.

findings.claim: The entire vNext pack cites zero existing ADRs, so it proposes a new canonical boundary without declaring supersession of any of the 18 recorded decisions it overrides — a direct violation of the project's lifecycle rules.
findings.evidence: `grep -rnoE "ADR-[0-9]{3}" docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/` → `(count: 0)`. The only in-repo artifact ID the pack cites at all is `PRD-073` (architecture/04-WORK-CONTRACT.md:27). By contrast the pack DOES declare GitHub-issue supersession precisely: FPV-05.md:42 "Existing #360 and #328 are closed or explicitly superseded by this implementation"; FPV-06.md:37; FPV-08.md:38. ADR-005 (status: active) line 104: "deprecated и superseded = TERMINAL" and its transition table line 77: "| active | superseded | `supersede --by NEW` | terminal |" — supersession is an explicit, commanded transition, not an implicit one.
findings.recommendation: Before FPV-01 opens, produce an explicit collision register: for each of ADR-001, 002, 003, 005, 006, 008, 009, 011, 012, 015, 016, 018 state one of {unaffected | amended | superseded-by-new-ADR}. Every `superseded` entry must name the successor and be executed via `forgeplan supersede <id> --by <new>` (RED LINE #11: MCP/CLI only). Add "names every ADR it supersedes" to FPV-01's acceptance criteria.

findings.claim: ADR-001 (ACTIVE) and ADR-009 (ACTIVE) already contradict each other in the repo today; FPV-01 cannot deliver "one canonical ADR" until a human adjudicates which of the two survives.
findings.evidence: ADR-001 title (line 11, `status: active` line 10): "No adapter traits — AI agent is the orchestrator, not Forgeplan". ADR-009 title (line 12, `status: active` line 11): "Forgeplan as orchestrator — Playbook Skill Agent Mapping Pack marketplace model", decision line 45: "**Forgeplan-core становится оркестратором** — знает **когда какой playbook запускать**, **кому делегировать каждый шаг**". Neither declares supersession: ADR-001 frontmatter links = `EPIC-002 refines`, `NOTE-009 supersedes` (lines 5-9); ADR-009 frontmatter links = `PROB-042 based_on`, `ADR-008 informs` (lines 6-10). FPV-01.md:33 requires "[ ] One canonical ADR is active and linked to the vNext Epic."
findings.recommendation: Treat this as a prerequisite issue ahead of FPV-01 (FPV-00.5). Run `forgeplan reason` / a human decision on the ADR-001 vs ADR-009 conflict, then supersede the loser. Do not let the vNext boundary ADR be the vehicle that silently resolves a pre-existing contradiction the pack never noticed.

findings.claim: The pack's adapter/ports architecture is the exact design ADR-001 (ACTIVE) rejected — core-side abstractions over external systems — and the pack neither cites nor supersedes it.
findings.evidence: ADR-001:30 "**Отвергаем adapter traits.** Forgeplan НЕ интегрируется напрямую с внешними системами (кроме LLM)."; :40 "**Loose coupling**: Forgeplan не знает о существовании Hindsight или Orchestra."; :46-47 rejected alternatives "**MCP-to-MCP calls** — отвергнуто" and "**Plugin system** — отвергнуто: complexity для minimal gain". Pack 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:80: "Core зависит от абстракций `ArtifactRepository`, `GitProvenanceProvider`, `EvidenceProvider`, `PolicyProvider`, `HostCapabilities`"; 09-ADAPTER-ARCHITECTURE.md:52-61 "Core предоставляет стабильные ports: ContractReader / ExecutionRegistrar / EvidenceSubmitter / VerdictReader / PolicyEvaluator / ExternalReferenceStore"; 11-ORCHESTRATOR-INTEGRATIONS.md:13-27 names Kandev, Vibe Kanban, Conductor, Paperclip as first-class adapter targets. Partial mitigation acknowledged: 09:63 "Adapter-specific API и config не входят в core crates" — so the concrete integrations stay out, but the abstractions do not. Note ADR-001 is only *partially* eroded already: RFC-003 (status: draft) shipped 7 storage/embed traits (`crates/forgeplan-core/src/driver/mod.rs:34,76,106,127,152,220,234`), but those are internal storage drivers, not the external-system traits ADR-001 named (MemoryProvider, CodeIndex, TaskTracker, NotificationSink) — so ADR-001 is NOT already superseded, and its status field says nothing of the kind.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: UNDECLARED_SUPERSESSION (with a CONTRADICTION core on the DIP section). FPV-01 must either (a) supersede ADR-001 with a successor ADR that states which of its five rationales no longer hold and why, or (b) narrow the pack's ports to demonstrably not be external-system integration traits. Silently shipping both is not an option — ADR-001 is cited as the reason core has "единственная external dep = LLM provider" (ADR-001:50).

findings.claim: The pack forbids ForgePlan from owning agent processes, but ADR-011 (ACTIVE) and shipped code have forgeplan-core spawning `claude --print` subprocesses today; the pack never mentions the playbook runtime it would have to delete.
findings.evidence: Pack 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:53 ownership table: "| Agent process, tools, model | Cursor, Codex, OpenCode, Claude Code |"; :36 "ForgePlan не является ... coding agent"; :40 "general-purpose workflow engine"; FPV-01.md:29 required decision "Agent execution and scheduling remain outside core." Against that: ADR-011 (`status: active`, line 8) title "Plugin/Agent dispatchers invoke `claude --print` directly", decision: "`PluginDispatcher` и `AgentDispatcher` invoke **`claude` CLI напрямую через `tokio::process::Command`**". Shipped: `crates/forgeplan-core/src/playbook/dispatch/agent_dispatcher.rs:69` `const DEFAULT_AGENT_BINARY: &str = "claude";`, plus `plugin_dispatcher.rs`, `claude_print.rs`, `skill_dispatcher.rs`, `command_dispatcher.rs` in the same directory, and CLI surfaces `crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/playbook.rs` + `ingest.rs`. The pack contains zero occurrences of "playbook", "ingest" or "dispatcher" outside FPV-01's single line about `forgeplan_dispatch`.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: CONTRADICTION. FPV-01 already flags `forgeplan_dispatch` (FPV-01.md:36) — extend that same explicit-ownership decision to cover the ADR-009/ADR-010/ADR-011 playbook runtime and its five dispatchers, with a stated migration and deprecation path. Deciding the boundary without naming the largest shipped violation of it will produce a boundary ADR that is false on day one.

findings.claim: ForgePlan already owns substantially more workspace/worktree/session state than the pack's boundary permits, and the pack contradicts itself on this point by placing claims/leases inside Core.
findings.evidence: Pack 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:38 "ForgePlan не является ... worktree manager"; :52 "| Workspace, worktree, branch, session | Agent host или orchestrator |"; 05-EXECUTION-RECEIPT.md:9-16 external owner owns "workspace/worktree; branch; session lifecycle". Against that, ADR-015 (`status: active`, line 18) decision: per-call `workspace` param + `FORGEPLAN_WORKSPACE` + "error response `-32602` когда detection видит multi-worktree env"; ADR-016 (`status: active`, line 18) invariants: "HIGH-1: ONE canonical path feeds both the store-cache key AND `acquire_workspace_lock`", "Reads are lock-free; writes serialize via per-workspace lock." Shipped: `crates/forgeplan-mcp/src/server.rs:386,413,440` (`resolve_workspace` / `resolve_workspace_read` / `resolve_workspace_core`), `crates/forgeplan-core/src/workspace/git.rs:30` (`git rev-parse --git-common-dir`), `crates/forgeplan-core/src/session/mod.rs:46` "Persisted session state in `.forgeplan/session.yaml`", `crates/forgeplan-core/src/claim/mod.rs:48,56` (`Claim { expires_at }`, TTL 1min..24h). And the pack's own 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:46 lists "- claims/leases;" as a **ForgePlan Core** component — i.e. execution-coordination state the boundary doc just assigned to orchestrators.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION plus an internal CONTRADICTION the pack must fix. FPV-01 must add an explicit carve-out row to the ownership matrix distinguishing "ForgePlan resolves which workspace a call addresses + leases artifact edits" (kept, per ADR-015/016) from "ForgePlan creates/manages worktrees" (rejected). Reconcile 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:46 with 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:52 before either is adopted.

findings.claim: The pack introduces four new persisted, immutable, digest-bearing document classes (WorkContract, ExecutionReceipt, EvidenceBundle, VerificationVerdict) without ever saying where they live — it never mentions markdown, LanceDB or `.forgeplan/`, so its compatibility with ADR-003 is undetermined.
findings.evidence: `grep -rni "markdown|source of truth|lancedb"` over the pack → zero hits; `grep -rn "\.forgeplan"` → one hit, in `prompts/ISSUE-BUILDER.md:8`, unrelated to storage. The only persistence language in the whole pack is FPV-04.md:16 "ExecutionReceipt persistence and retrieval" and FPV-05.md:23 "EvidenceBundle persistence/schema" — neither says where. Against ADR-003 (`status: active`, line 8): "**Инвертировать direction of truth**: Markdown файлы = единственный source of truth. LanceDB = index/cache layer." (line 25) and "rm -rf lance/ → не страшно, reindex восстановит всё из .md файлов" (line 50). The new classes are structurally hostile to a hand-editable markdown store: work-contract.schema.json requires `digest` (minLength 16) and integer `version`, and 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:103-104 mandates "1. WorkContract immutable после начала исполнения. 2. Scope expansion создаёт новую версию контракта."
findings.recommendation: Verdict: NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION — blocks FPV-03, not FPV-01. Add a storage section to 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md answering: are compiled contracts (a) git-committed JSON under `.forgeplan/contracts/`, (b) recomputable-on-demand and never persisted, or (c) a second authoritative store? Option (c) breaks ADR-003 and would need an explicit ADR-003 amendment. Note ADR-018:38-42 already refused to introduce "второй authoritative не-markdown стор" for exactly this reason — reuse that reasoning rather than relitigating it.

findings.claim: FPV-15's optional server with multi-repository registry, event ingestion and replay duplicates ADR-018's SpaceJournal + ForgeMesh design, which is in-flight draft work on the current branch and which explicitly rejected the server-shaped topology for now.
findings.evidence: FPV-15.md:17-25 scope: "Streamable HTTP MCP/API", "event ingestion with idempotency", "multi-repository registry", "subscriptions/webhooks", "replay/recovery for integration events". ADR-018 (`status: draft`, line 12, `last_modified_at: 2026-07-25`) delivers the same capability set locally: "**SpaceJournal (H3) = durable transport + emit**" (line 78), "**ForgeMesh (H4) = addressing/read plane**" (line 85), cascade "explicit > registry.json > walkdir" (line 88), "`space_subscribe` с since-cursor" (line 96), "**Durable catch-up:** подписчик, отключившийся на сутки, догоняет пропущенное по since-cursor" (line 135). ADR-018 explicitly deferred the server/broker form: "**H2 SpaceBus** — встроенный брокер ... **не выживает**" (line 71) and "**best_use_case:** когда single-machine перестанет быть single-machine (сеть, контейнеры, remote-агенты, «ForgePlan Teams/Cloud»); до тех пор отложено" (line 243). The pack never cites ADR-018, PRD-081 or SPEC-006. Recent commit on this branch: `99d0cf0 docs(prd,adr,spec,evid): shape space-mesh cross-project layer`.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: NEEDS_HUMAN_DECISION. Two designs for one capability is the failure mode ADR-018 was written to avoid. Either FPV-15 declares itself the multi-machine successor ADR-018 already scoped as future (and cites it), or ADR-018's F2 absorbs FPV-15. Add ADR-018/PRD-081/SPEC-006 to FPV-15's dependency list; FPV-15 currently lists only `FPV-02, FPV-04, FPV-05, FPV-07, FPV-09`.

findings.claim: FPV-06's claim-centric R_eff silently amends the weakest-link invariant recorded in ADR-006 (ACTIVE) and codified in CLAUDE.md, and leaves ADR-002's skip-non-active-dependencies rule unaddressed.
findings.evidence: ADR-006:57 Invariants: "- **R_eff = min(evidence_scores)** — weakest link principle НИКОГДА не average". CLAUDE.md:682: "`R_eff = min(evidence_scores)` — trust = weakest link, **never average**". Pack 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:66: "R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)" and :69 "Informational claims не обрушивают весь decision score." The min operator survives but its **domain narrows** from all linked evidence to required claims only — a behavioral change to an active ADR invariant. ADR-002 (`status: active`, line 5) decision: "**R_eff пропускает non-active зависимости** (draft, deprecated, superseded) при рекурсивном вычислении" — the pack's claim model has no dependency-recursion concept at all, so it is silent on whether this rule survives. FPV-06 does acknowledge a compatibility gap ("Document whether R_eff v2 is opt-in, schema-version gated or introduced by major version") but names neither ADR.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: UNDECLARED_SUPERSESSION. FPV-06 must add an amendment to ADR-006 (like ADR-003's Amendment 1/2 pattern) stating the new min-domain, and must state explicitly whether ADR-002's recursive skip rule is retained, replaced by claim-level required/informational, or dropped. Also update CLAUDE.md:682 in the same PR or the documented formula becomes stale.

findings.claim: The pack introduces two new status vocabularies that collide token-for-token with ADR-005's artifact lifecycle, and adds an authority precondition to `artifact.activate` that ADR-005's state machine does not have.
findings.evidence: ADR-005 (`status: active`, line 8) statuses: draft / active / stale / superseded / deprecated, with "deprecated и superseded = TERMINAL" (:104) and transition "| draft | active | `activate` | validation gate |" (:74). Pack 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:44-50 verdicts: "accepted / rejected / incomplete / blocked / requires_human_review / **stale**". Pack 05-EXECUTION-RECEIPT.md:36-46 receipt statuses: "registered / running / blocked / awaiting_review / completed / failed / cancelled / expired / **superseded**". So `stale` means both "artifact's valid_until expired" (ADR-005) and "this verification is out of date" (pack); `superseded` means both a TERMINAL artifact status and a non-terminal receipt status. Separately, 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:31 lists `artifact.activate` as a policy-gated action and :51 "Human principal утверждает contract и final verdict" / :47 "Builder и verifier обязаны быть разными actor instances" — new preconditions on a transition ADR-005 defines as gated only by validation.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: CONTRADICTION (vocabulary) + UNDECLARED_SUPERSESSION (activation gate). Namespace the new vocabularies (`verdict.stale`, `receipt.superseded`) in Protocol v1 schemas so JSON consumers cannot conflate them with artifact lifecycle, and file an ADR-005 amendment describing the added authority precondition on `activate` and how `blocked` / `requires_human_review` map onto the five artifact statuses.

findings.claim: The pack's host-integration set silently drops four harnesses that ADR-008 (ACTIVE) committed to and that are partly shipped, without any deprecation decision.
findings.evidence: ADR-008 (`status: active`, line 6) Decision §5 commits to a cross-harness table (lines 39-45): Claude Code, **Cursor, Windsurf, Cline, Roo, GitHub Copilot**, agentskills.io generic — "out-of-the-box работа в 7+ harness'ах" (:65). Shipped subset: `crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/mcp.rs:29` — `bail!("unknown MCP client: '{other}' (supported: claude, cursor, windsurf)")`. The pack's 10-HOST-INTEGRATIONS.md covers only Cursor (:3), Codex (:19), OpenCode (:35), Claude Code (:46) and Generic MCP/AGENTS.md (:50); FPV-12.md ships "Cursor, Codex and OpenCode" only. Windsurf, Cline, Roo and Copilot appear nowhere in the pack. FPV-11.md:38 requires "[ ] Deprecated plugins have machine-readable replacement and sunset metadata" — but no decision to deprecate them is anywhere in the pack.
findings.recommendation: Verdict: UNDECLARED_SUPERSESSION. FPV-11/FPV-12 must state explicitly whether Windsurf/Cline/Roo/Copilot are (a) retained at `generic MCP/AGENTS.md` conformance tier, or (b) deprecated — and if (b), amend or supersede ADR-008 rather than letting the surface shrink by omission. Note ADR-008's own Weakest Link already caps trust at CL2 pending the agentskills.io spec, so this is exactly the axis it flagged as volatile.

findings.claim: Marketplace v2's seven extension categories replace ADR-009's five-primitive marketplace model (Playbook/Skill/Agent/Mapping/Pack) with no home for the shipped Playbook, Mapping and Ingest primitives, and without declaring supersession.

findings.claim: FPV-03's deterministic-digest requirement collides with ADR-012's slug/display-number duality: the same artifact's `id` changes at CI merge time, so an identical graph would produce a different contract digest.
findings.evidence: FPV-03/04-WORK-CONTRACT.md compiler must "выдать deterministic canonical representation" (04:43) and FPV-03.md AC: "Repeated compilation against identical graph/revision produces identical canonical digest." `protocol/schemas/work-contract.schema.json` requires `source.artifacts[]` items with `{id, digest}` where `id` is an unqualified string. findings.claim: The WorkContract compiler's step "find active decisions applicable to affected paths/domain" has no machine-readable data source in the current ADR corpus: no ADR carries affected-paths metadata, one ADR has no frontmatter at all, and four of eighteen are draft.

area: vNext central idea — product boundary and target architecture (docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/architecture/01 + 02) stress-tested against shipped v0.33.0
summary: The boundary is not a description of ForgePlan — it is an undeclared demolition order. Sixteen shipped CLI surfaces (leases, dispatch, order/blocked, progress, phase state machine, session state, estimate/calibrate, remember/recall, playbook runtime with `claude --print` agent spawning) fall inside the pack's own "ForgePlan не является" list, and the pack names exactly one of them (`dispatch`) and leaves even that undecided. The pack contradicts four ACTIVE ADRs (ADR-001 rejects adapter traits; ADR-009 makes core the orchestrator; ADR-010/011 make core spawn agents; ADR-017 makes core depend on a concrete host binary) while containing zero references to any `.forgeplan/` artifact ID — no supersede, no acknowledgement. Its two headline principles are self-refuted inside the pack: "One owner per state" is violated three times in the ownership matrix itself, and the Liskov claim is contradicted by the pack's own `advisory`/`unsupported` enforcement levels. The one genuinely new capability — verifying git provenance instead of scoring agent-authored prose — is real and measurable (148 EvidencePacks, 0 contain any SHA, 0 provenance code in scoring), but it is 2 of 16 issues and does not require the repositioning that the other 14 carry.

findings.claim: The boundary's 'ForgePlan не является' list retires sixteen shipped CLI surfaces, and the pack names exactly one of them (`dispatch`, left undecided) — the migration cost is never stated anywhere in the pack.
findings.evidence: 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md:34,38,39,40,42 forbid 'task tracker', 'worktree manager', 'scheduler', 'general-purpose workflow engine', 'memory platform общего назначения'. Shipped today (81 top-level subcommands in crates/forgeplan-cli/src/main.rs): claim.rs / claims.rs / release.rs (leases + assignee — `.forgeplan/claims/RFC-011.yaml` holds `agent_id: claude-code/opus-4.7/architect-reviewer-task-rfc011-blog`, `expires_at`, `note`), dispatch.rs (N-agent bucket scheduler), order.rs + blocked.rs (backlog sequencing), progress.rs (checkbox burndown across all artifacts), phase.rs + phase_advance.rs (`.forgeplan/state/ADR-018.yaml`: `current_phase: validate` with transition history = a Kanban column), session.rs (`.forgeplan/session.yaml`: `phase: routing`, `active_artifact: ADR-015`), estimate.rs + calibrate.rs (Fibonacci × grade PM estimation), remember.rs + recall.rs (`--category fact|convention|procedure|insight`, `.forgeplan/memory/*.md` — a general memory platform), playbook.rs (48KB sequential workflow engine). `rg -n 'dispatch|claim|worktree|playbook|progress' -g '*.md'` across the whole pack returns ONE hit for dispatch (issues/forgeplan/FPV-01.md:21 'Decide whether current dispatch scheduling remains core...') and ZERO hits for playbook, progress, order, blocked, session, estimate, remember.
findings.recommendation: Before FPV-01 can be an executable Wave-0 gate, add a disposition table with one row per shipped surface: KEEP / MOVE-TO-EXTENSION / DEPRECATE-WITH-WINDOW / REMOVE, each with the semver impact and the replacement. FPV-01's AC currently covers only `forgeplan_dispatch` (FPV-01.md:36) — widen it to the full list or the boundary ships as aspiration while the binary contradicts it.

findings.location: docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/ (whole pack) vs .forgeplan/adrs/ADR-001, ADR-009, ADR-010, ADR-011, ADR-017 (all status: active)

A boundary ADR that silently overrides five active ADRs is not a decision, it is a fork of the decision graph.

findings.claim: The WorkContract compiler is specified to compile fields that do not exist in the canonical graph, so on this repo's own reference corpus it must either refuse for ~half of PRDs or infer — and inference breaks its own determinism and provenance requirements.
findings.evidence: 04-WORK-CONTRACT.md:12-24 requires 'allowed and forbidden paths', 'acceptance criteria with stable IDs', 'required Evidence by criterion'; :35-45 requires 'выдать deterministic canonical representation' and 'объяснить происхождение каждого contract field'. Measured on `.forgeplan/prds/` (65 PRDs, the dogfood reference corpus): `rg -l '^## Affected Files' prds/ | wc -l` → 33; `rg -l '^## Acceptance Criteria' prds/ | wc -l` → 37; `rg -ril 'forbidden.?path' .forgeplan | wc -l` → 0; `rg -l 'required.evidence|Evidence Requirements' prds/ | wc -l` → 0. `templates/prd/_TEMPLATE.md` has no forbidden-paths and no per-criterion evidence section at all.
findings.recommendation: Insert a backfill/migration issue BEFORE FPV-03 in EXECUTION-ORDER.md Wave 2: extend the PRD/RFC/Spec templates with `forbidden_paths` and per-AC `required_evidence`, add a validator MUST for them, and specify what `contract compile` does for legacy artifacts (refuse vs partial contract with declared gaps). Without it FPV-03's acceptance ('deterministic compile подтверждён golden tests') can only be met on synthetic fixtures, and the whole Wave 2-5 chain rests on it.

findings.claim: FORGE principle O ('One owner per state') is falsified three times inside the ownership matrix it introduces, and worktree/session ownership is double-assigned across two architecture documents.
findings.evidence: 01:85 «**O — One owner per state.** Для каждого состояния существует один источник истины.» Yet in the table headed 'Канонический владелец': :50 'Business goals, org, budgets | Paperclip **или** бизнес-система' (disjunction); :51 'Task backlog, priority, assignee | Linear, Jira, Kandev, Vibe Kanban' (four owners); :52 'Workspace, worktree, branch, session | Agent host **или** orchestrator' (disjunction). The disjunction on :52 then resolves into a direct conflict: 10-HOST-INTEGRATIONS.md:17 'Cursor владеет worktree, sandbox и session' vs 11-ORCHESTRATOR-INTEGRATIONS.md:19 'Vibe Kanban владеет issue, workspace/worktree, agent session' and :23 'Conductor владеет workspace, session, harness, terminal'. When Vibe Kanban or Conductor launches Cursor into a worktree — the pack's own headline topology (02:5-20 stacks orchestrators ABOVE hosts) — both documents claim the same state. Second double-assignment: 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE.md:46 lists 'claims/leases' as a **ForgePlan Core** component while 01:51 assigns 'assignee' to external trackers; a TTL lease naming an `agent_id` IS an assignee record (`.forgeplan/claims/RFC-011.yaml`).
findings.recommendation: Make every matrix cell name exactly one owner, and add a resolution rule for the nested case ('the innermost system that created the worktree owns it; the outer system holds an opaque reference'). Then either move leases out of Core per :51, or amend :51 to 'ForgePlan owns short-lived execution leases; external trackers own durable assignment' — but say it once, in the matrix.

findings.claim: The word 'claim' carries three incompatible meanings inside one pack, and FPV-08 reuses the exact name of a shipped MCP tool for a different concept — Protocol v1 schemas and the agent API will be ambiguous by construction.
findings.evidence: Sense 1 — verifiable assertion: 06:33 'найти required claim'; 06:65-66 'claim_score = evaluate(...)  R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)'; 01:18 'claims и risks'. Sense 2 — coordination lease: 02:46 'claims/leases' as a Core component, i.e. the shipped `.forgeplan/claims/<ID>.yaml` written by crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/claim.rs:94-99. Sense 3 — authority permission: 07:27 '- execution.claim;'. Then 08-AGENT-API-AND-MCP.md:17 publishes `forgeplan_claim` in the 9-verb agent API — a name already bound in the shipped 73-tool MCP surface to the lease operation (crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/claim.rs doc-comment: 'Mirrors the `forgeplan_claim` MCP tool').
findings.recommendation: Rename before FPV-02 freezes the schemas: `Claim` → `Assertion` (or `Criterion`) for the verification concept, keep `Lease` for coordination, and rename the authority action to `execution.acquire_lease`. Whatever `forgeplan_claim` means in v2 must not silently change meaning for existing callers — the marketplace cookbook skill documents all 73 current tools by name.

findings.claim: The Liskov claim ('One WorkContract has identical semantics in Cursor, Codex, OpenCode and Claude Code') is refuted by the pack's own enforcement-level taxonomy, and Claude Code — the only host ForgePlan ships for today — is excluded from the test that would check it.
findings.evidence: 01:72 asserts identical semantics across four hosts. 07:56-61 defines enforcement levels including «`advisory` — только предупреждение» and «`unsupported` — host не может обеспечить правило»; 16:42-48 defines capability levels full/partial/advisory/unsupported/experimental; 09:36-46 requires each adapter to declare 'pre-edit enforcement', 'command enforcement', 'worktree awareness' as VARIABLE capabilities. A contract whose forbidden-path rule is blocked pre-edit on one host and merely warned about on another does not have identical semantics — it has identical text and different behaviour, which is precisely the substitutability failure Liskov names. Compounding: 16:27 'Один fixture WorkContract выполняется минимум в **Cursor, Codex и OpenCode**' and 18:27 'Cursor, Codex и OpenCode прошли Host Conformance v1' — Claude Code, named in the Liskov claim at 01:72 and the only host with a shipped integration (`forgeplan mcp install --client claude`), appears in neither the portability test nor the release gate.
findings.recommendation: Split the claim into what is actually host-independent and what is not: (a) 'the VerificationVerdict for a given EvidenceBundle is computed core-side and is byte-identical across hosts' — defensible, testable, and the real value; (b) 'PREVENTION semantics vary by declared enforcement level and MUST be surfaced in the CapabilityManifest' — honest. Delete the unqualified Liskov sentence. Add Claude Code to 16:27 and 18:27 or explicitly state why the reference integration is exempt.

findings.claim: 'Core does not become a scheduler' is incoherent both backwards (a sequential job runner with budgets and timeouts already ships in core) and forwards (FPV-15 builds a durable event service with retries and replay, then declares scheduling a non-goal by label).
findings.evidence: Shipped: crates/forgeplan-core/src/playbook/types.rs:179-197 `pub enum Delegation { Plugin, Agent, Skill, Command { command: Vec<String> }, ForgeplanCore }` — arbitrary shell command execution is a first-class delegation type; :150-170 per-step `timeout_seconds`, `budget_usd` ('Plugin and Agent dispatchers translate this to `--max-budget-usd <N>`'), `allowed_tools` ('Translated to `--allowedTools <T1> <T2> ...`'). That is a job runner with resource governance. Proposed: FPV-15.md:14-23 scope includes 'event ingestion with idempotency', 'subscriptions/webhooks', 'replay/recovery for integration events', 'audit log'; FPV-15.md:28-29 then lists 'launching agent processes' and 'task scheduling' as non-goals. An idempotent, replayable, webhook-driven event service that correlates external runs is a scheduler in every property except the label. Meanwhile FPV-01.md:21 leaves the shipped scheduler's fate open ('Decide whether current dispatch scheduling remains core...') and FPV-01.md:36 makes that an unchecked AC — the Wave-0 gate depends on a decision the pack declines to make.
findings.recommendation: State the discriminator in mechanism, not in vocabulary: 'ForgePlan never decides WHEN work runs or WHO runs it; it may execute a caller-initiated, bounded, synchronous step.' Then measure the playbook runtime against it — `Delegation::Command` and `Delegation::Agent` fail that test and must move to an extension. And decide `dispatch` inside FPV-01 rather than deferring it, since FPV-01 is the gate for every other wave.

findings.claim: The boundary retroactively places shipped v0.33.0 workspace/session machinery outside ForgePlan, and it conflates 'owning worktrees' with 'being worktree-aware' — leaving no rule for the thing that actually caused the user-reported bug.
findings.evidence: 01:52 assigns 'Workspace, worktree, branch, session' to 'Agent host или orchestrator'. Shipped and active: ADR-015 (active) Decision — «H1 (PRIMARY): per-call `workspace` параметр на mutating MCP tools + `FORGEPLAN_WORKSPACE` env var (H2) с resolution chain `param → env → cwd`»; ADR-016 (active) Implementation Note — «`ForgeplanServer::resolve_workspace_core(param, policy)` is the one resolution chain … `DetectionPolicy` enum parameterizes read-vs-write». Session state ships as ForgePlan-owned data: `.forgeplan/session.yaml` contains `phase: routing`, `active_artifact: ADR-015`, `route_depth: standard` plus a 20-entry transition history; crates/forgeplan-core/src/session/ defines `pub struct SessionState { phase, active_artifact, route_depth, phase_started_at, history }`. ADR-015 Context records the driving user runs «**19 worktrees параллельно**» — the problem was never 'who owns the worktree', it was 'which workspace does ForgePlan write into', which the boundary does not address at all.
findings.recommendation: Add a matrix row that separates the two: 'Worktree lifecycle (create/destroy) → host/orchestrator' and 'Workspace resolution for ForgePlan writes → ForgePlan (per-call param, strict on ambiguity)'. Then either grandfather `.forgeplan/session.yaml` as ForgePlan-internal methodology state (it tracks methodology phase, not an agent session) or schedule its removal — currently the boundary makes an active, user-driven, three-artifact decision chain illegal by omission.

findings.claim: The authority engine's binding rules rest on unauthenticated, self-declared actor identity, which the pack explicitly refuses to implement — making invariant 6 and the builder≠verifier rule advisory by construction rather than 'проверяемая domain policy'.
findings.evidence: 02:108 states as an unconditional invariant: 'Critical execution не может быть принято тем же actor, который его выполнял.' FPV-07.md ACs require 'Deep/Critical policy can require a different verifier actor instance' and 'Agents cannot change the policy governing their active execution'. FPV-07.md Non-goals then removes the substrate: 'User directory or enterprise IAM implementation; actor identities may be supplied by adapters/providers.' 07-AUTHORITY-POLICY.md:2 frames the goal as 'Перенести критические ограничения из prompts/hooks в **проверяемую** domain policy'. The shipped precedent shows what self-declared identity is worth: `claim::validate_agent_id` (crates/forgeplan-core/src/claim/mod.rs:178-190) checks only emptiness, length and character class — any caller passes any `--agent`. Identity is already brittle in a single round-trip: crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/claim.rs:27 defaults to `format!("cli-{}", ...)` while crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/release.rs:14 defaults to `format!("cli/{}", ...)`, so bare `forgeplan claim X` then `forgeplan release X` hits `ClaimError::NotHeldByRequester` (mod.rs:411-421).
findings.recommendation: Either add an attestation substrate (signed git commits / CI-issued OIDC actor tokens / host-adapter-signed receipts) as an explicit FPV-07 dependency, or downgrade 02:108 from 'Неизменяемый инвариант' to 'enforceable at `ci` and `full` levels; `advisory` where the actor is self-declared' and say so in the CapabilityManifest. Also fix the `cli-` / `cli/` default-agent asymmetry — it is a live demonstration that identity is currently a formatting accident.

findings.location: whole pack vs .forgeplan/problems/ (77 artifacts) and .forgeplan/evidence/ (148 artifacts)
findings.claim: The repositioning is one-eighth necessary and seven-eighths unmotivated: the provenance-verification gap (FPV-05/FPV-06) is real and unfixable with today's ForgePlan, but the host/orchestrator/marketplace/web/server half has zero demand evidence in a 77-problem corpus.
findings.evidence: STEELMAN FOR — the gap is real and measurable. `ls .forgeplan/evidence/ | wc -l` → 148; `rg -l 'base_sha|commit_sha|result_sha' .forgeplan/evidence/ | wc -l` → 0; `rg -n 'base_sha|result_sha|git_delta|provenance' crates/forgeplan-core/src/scoring/` → no matches; `templates/evidence/_TEMPLATE.md` carries only `evidence_type`, `verdict`, `congruence_level` (lines 23-25) — all agent-authored prose. So R_eff today is `min()` over a set of self-assertions, which is exactly what 06-EVIDENCE-AND-VERIFICATION.md:5 targets: 'Verify the artifact, not the claim.' The project's own methodology already concedes it: CLAUDE.md RED LINE #5 'Silent failures (PROB-035, PROB-039) все от того что протестировали только happy path' and Task List Discipline 'Агент, помечающий собственную задачу готовой, выносит **утверждение**, а не вердикт'. Today's ForgePlan structurally cannot close this — that is genuine new capability, not a rename. STEELMAN AGAINST — it is 2 of 16 issues, and it needs no repositioning: `git diff --name-only <base>..<result>` + a scope check + three evidence frontmatter fields would do it inside the current architecture. The other 14 issues (Protocol v1 versioning, Cursor/Codex/OpenCode adapters, Marketplace v2, Web v2, site rewrite, optional server) have no filed demand: across 77 problems, `rg -il 'cursor|codex|opencode|work.?contract|execution.?receipt|provenance'` matches 4 files, and every match is unrelated — PROB-037:65 'forgeplan mcp install --client claude # или cursor / windsurf' (installer targets), PROB-042:21 (reference-plugin harness compat), PROB-022:58 (a wish-list bullet), PROB-026:71 (a module-placement nit). The actual recent user pain is PROB-072 (worktree projection drift), PROB-073 ('прям радует результат / только сука медленно'), PROB-077 (silent data loss via `@file`), PROB-078 (stale read-after-write) — all local correctness, none addressed by repositioning.
findings.recommendation: Split the program. Ship FPV-05 (git-provenance verification) and FPV-06 (claim-centric R_eff) NOW as a normal PRD→RFC→ADR cycle against today's boundary — they need no protocol, no adapters, no server, and they close a gap you can measure at 0/148. Gate the boundary/positioning half (FPV-09..FPV-15) behind at least one filed PROB from an external user describing cross-host contract portability pain. Right now the pack's most valuable idea is buried under fifteen issues that no problem artifact asked for.

findings.claim: FPV-01's acceptance criteria mandate placing the canonical boundary decision in `docs/`, which the project's authoritative methodology forbids — and the pack has already pre-placed it there before any ADR exists.
findings.evidence: FPV-01.md:34: '- [ ] `docs/architecture/product-boundary.md` exists and includes ownership matrix.' CLAUDE.md:174: '| Решения | `.forgeplan/adrs/` | ADR — **единственное** место; `docs/` держит гайды и схемы, не решения |'. The decision content already lives at docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/architecture/01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY.md ('## Каноническое определение', '## Владение состояниями'), untracked — `git log --oneline -3 -- docs/vnext` returns nothing, and `ls ref/` shows the source 'ForgePlan Agent Pack.zip'.
findings.recommendation: Rewrite FPV-01.md:34 as: the canonical boundary is an ADR in `.forgeplan/adrs/` created via `forgeplan new adr` (RED LINE #11); `docs/architecture/product-boundary.md` may exist only as a generated or explicitly-derivative reader's guide that cites the ADR ID. Otherwise the program's first act is a methodology violation by its own tooling.

findings.claim: The 9-verb agent API replaces a 73-tool shipped surface with no deprecation window, no mapping table and no compatibility policy — while the pack writes a detailed compatibility policy for schemas only.
findings.evidence: 08:9-19 lists nine tools (`forgeplan_next`, `forgeplan_context`, `forgeplan_contract`, `forgeplan_claim`, `forgeplan_execution`, `forgeplan_evidence`, `forgeplan_verify`, `forgeplan_status`, `forgeplan_search`). Shipped surface: `bash scripts/check-mcp-tool-count.sh` → 'Actual MCP tool count (src): 73'; `rg -c '#\[tool\(' crates/forgeplan-mcp/src/server.rs` → 73. 03-PROTOCOL-V1.md:20-26 defines a full semver compatibility policy — but only for Protocol documents, nothing for the tool surface. Downstream breakage is concrete: the marketplace `fpl-skills:forgeplan-cookbook` skill documents the tool set by name for agents.
findings.recommendation: Add to FPV-08 an old→new tool mapping table, a deprecation window (tools remain callable and emit a `Next:` hint pointing at the v2 verb for at least one minor release), and a CI drift check extending `scripts/check-mcp-tool-count.sh` to assert every retired tool has a mapping row.

area: vNext issue pack: governance compliance, dependency DAG, acceptance-criteria testability, sizing, and md↔JSON consistency across FPV-00..FPV-15
summary: The 16 issues are internally coherent as prose and the declared dependency graph is acyclic with no forward (later-phase) edges — those two checks pass. Everything else about the issue layer fails its own contract. Zero of 16 issues satisfy the required-section list the pack itself publishes in ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md (Product boundary 0/16, Rollback-migration 0/16, Evidence 2/16, Dependencies 0/16 in body, Scope 8/16, Non-goals 7/16), and the pack's own validate_pack.py never checks sections, cycles, phase ordering, or md↔JSON drift, so nothing in the toolchain can catch this. The program carries four mutually contradictory sequencing authorities (manifest phases, FPV-00 "Delivery phases", 17-ROADMAP "Phase 0-6", EXECUTION-ORDER "Waves") that disagree on where FPV-06, FPV-08, FPV-10 and FPV-12 belong, and EXECUTION-ORDER declares FPV-07 parallel to FPV-03 while the manifest declares FPV-07 dependent on it. Most seriously, the pack contains zero references to any existing ADR while proposing core ports that active ADR-001 explicitly rejected — it has no supersession plan for the decisions it overturns.

findings.claim: Zero of the 16 issue bodies satisfy the required-section list that the pack's own ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md mandates; three of the eight required sections appear in essentially no issue at all.
findings.evidence: ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:23-32 requires 'Objective / Product boundary / Scope / Non-goals / Dependencies / Acceptance criteria / Evidence / Rollback/migration where applicable'. Heading extraction over issues/bodies.json gives: FPV-00 ['Objective','Canonical product definition','Program outcomes','Non-goals','Delivery phases','Definition of Done']; FPV-01 ['Problem','Scope','Required decisions','Acceptance Criteria','Evidence']; FPV-02 ['Objective','Required protocol types','Scope','Acceptance Criteria','Non-goals']; FPV-03 ['Objective','Compiler inputs','Required commands/API','Acceptance Criteria','Non-goals']; FPV-04 ['Objective','Scope','Acceptance Criteria','Non-goals']; FPV-05 ['Objective','Existing work to incorporate','Scope','Acceptance Criteria','Evidence']; FPV-06 ['Objective','Existing work to incorporate','Model','Acceptance Criteria','Compatibility']; FPV-07 ['Objective','Scope','Acceptance Criteria','Non-goals']; FPV-08 ['Objective','Existing issues to incorporate','Required profiles','High-level operations','Acceptance Criteria']; FPV-09 ['Objective','Host checks','Orchestrator checks','Acceptance Criteria']; FPV-10 ['Objective','Canonical messaging','Scope','Acceptance Criteria','Important']; FPV-11 ['Objective','Categories','Scope','Acceptance Criteria']; FPV-12 ['Objective','Cursor deliverables','Codex deliverables','OpenCode deliverables','Acceptance Criteria','Non-goals']; FPV-13 ['Objective','Ownership rules','Deliverables','Acceptance Criteria']; FPV-14 ['Objective','Views','Boundary','Acceptance Criteria']; FPV-15 ['Objective','Scope','Explicit non-goals','Acceptance Criteria']. Totals: Objective 15/16 (FPV-01 uses 'Problem'), Product boundary 0/16 exact (3 near-synonyms: FPV-00 'Canonical product definition', FPV-13 'Ownership rules', FPV-14 'Boundary'), Scope 8/16 (missing in FPV-00/03/06/08/09/12/13/14), Non-goals 7/16 (missing in FPV-01/05/06/08/09/10/11/13/14), Dependencies 0/16 in body, Acceptance criteria 15/16 (FPV-00 has prose 'Definition of Done', no checkboxes), Evidence 2/16 (FPV-01, FPV-05 only), Rollback/migration 0/16 (FPV-06 '## Compatibility' is the only partial).
findings.recommendation: Either add the missing sections to all 16 bodies or amend ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md to a list the pack actually intends to meet. Then extend validate_pack.py to enforce the section list programmatically (see F12) so the contract is machine-checked before create_github_issues.py runs. Priority sections: Rollback/migration for the behaviour-breaking issues (FPV-05 activation gate, FPV-06 R_eff v2, FPV-07 policy enforcement, FPV-08 tool-surface reduction, FPV-10 docs IA/URL restructure), and Evidence for the 14 issues lacking it.

findings.claim: The program ships four mutually contradictory sequencing authorities; no single artifact is the ordering source of truth, and the issue-creation script publishes one of them into the epic while linking readers to a different one.
findings.evidence: (1) manifest.json puts FPV-10 at 'phase': 1 (issues/manifest.json:112) and FPV-08/FPV-06 at 'phase': 2 (manifest.json:87-93, :64-71). (2) governance/EXECUTION-ORDER.md:3-6 puts FPV-10 in 'Wave 0 — Alignment'. (3) architecture/17-ROADMAP.md:3-9 'Phase 0 — Product truth and correctness' includes 'закрыть критический CLI/MCP parity и JSON gaps' (= FPV-08) and 'устранить scoring/decay correctness blockers' (= FPV-06), i.e. two phases earlier than the manifest; 17-ROADMAP.md 'Phase 3 — Extensions' lists 'Cursor adapter; Codex adapter; OpenCode adapter' while manifest.json:133 puts FPV-12 at phase 4; 17-ROADMAP 'Phase 5' lists 'website rewrite' while manifest puts docs/positioning FPV-10 at phase 1. (4) issues/forgeplan/FPV-00.md:38-46 'Delivery phases' is a 1-7 list whose item 4 is 'Agent API and conformance' — the manifest splits those across phases 2 and 3. create_github_issues.py:119-126 emits '### Phase {phase}' headings from the manifest into the epic body, then create_github_issues.py:128-131 appends 'See ... EXECUTION-ORDER.md', pointing the reader at a contradicting order.
findings.recommendation: Declare manifest.json the single ordering authority, regenerate EXECUTION-ORDER.md and architecture/17-ROADMAP.md from it (or delete their phase lists and link to the manifest), and rewrite FPV-00's 'Delivery phases' as a generated section. Until then no agent can answer 'what is next' deterministically — which is exactly what next_issue.py claims to do.

findings.claim: The pack contains no reference to any existing ADR, yet it proposes core-level ports that active ADR-001 explicitly rejected and persistence of three new entity types with no reconciliation against active ADR-003; there is no supersession plan for the decisions it overturns.
findings.evidence: grep -rn 'ADR-0' over the whole pack returns zero hits (only the eight GitHub issue numbers appear in 'supersede' contexts: ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:48, FPV-05.md:42, FPV-06.md:37, FPV-08.md:38). Meanwhile .forgeplan/adrs/ADR-001-...md:10 'status: active' and :30 '**Отвергаем adapter traits.** Forgeplan НЕ интегрируется напрямую с внешними системами (кроме LLM).' — while architecture/09-ADAPTER-ARCHITECTURE.md:50-60 states 'Core предоставляет стабильные ports: ContractReader / ExecutionRegistrar / EvidenceSubmitter / VerdictReader / PolicyEvaluator / ExternalReferenceStore', and FPV-15 (repo ForgePlan/forgeplan) scopes 'subscriptions/webhooks' plus AC 'Server can correlate Paperclip/Kandev/Conductor events'. ADR-009 ('Forgeplan as orchestrator', status: active, line 11) collides with FPV-01's required decision 'Agent execution and scheduling remain outside core'. ADR-003 ('Markdown files as source of truth', status: active, line 8) is never addressed although FPV-03 compiles an immutable versioned WorkContract and FPV-04.md:16 requires 'ExecutionReceipt persistence and retrieval' with no storage substrate named anywhere in the pack. Separately, CLAUDE.md's layer table states ADRs in .forgeplan/adrs/ are the *only* home for decisions and 'docs/ держит гайды и схемы, не решения', yet 18 decision documents live in docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/architecture/.
findings.recommendation: Before FPV-01 opens: (a) enumerate every active ADR the vNext boundary contradicts (at minimum ADR-001, ADR-003, ADR-009) and add explicit `forgeplan supersede` steps to FPV-01's scope with the new canonical ADR as the superseder; (b) add a storage decision (markdown-primary vs new store) for WorkContract / ExecutionReceipt / EvidenceBundle to FPV-02 or FPV-03, since RED LINE #8 forbids direct LanceStore writes from commands and no projection path is specified; (c) migrate the architecture/*.md decision content into .forgeplan/adrs/ artifacts via MCP/CLI, leaving docs/vnext as guides only.

findings.claim: EXECUTION-ORDER.md declares FPV-07 executable in parallel with FPV-03, while manifest.json declares FPV-07 dependent on FPV-03 — the same contradiction recurs for FPV-11/FPV-09.
findings.evidence: governance/EXECUTION-ORDER.md:16-22 'Parallel after FPV-02: FPV-03 WorkContract. FPV-04 ExecutionReceipt. FPV-06 R_eff v2 ... FPV-07 Authority Policy. FPV-08 ...'. issues/manifest.json:76-83 declares FPV-07 with '"depends": ["FPV-02", "FPV-03"]'. Likewise EXECUTION-ORDER.md:28-31 'Wave 3 — Conformance and Extensions foundation: FPV-09 Conformance. FPV-11 Marketplace v2.' while manifest.json:122-127 declares FPV-11 '"depends": ["FPV-02", "FPV-09"]' with both at phase 3.
findings.recommendation: Either drop FPV-03 from FPV-07's depends (if AuthorityPolicy only needs the FPV-02 schema, which the drafts suggest — work-contract.schema.json already carries an 'authority' block) or move FPV-07 to a 'Then:' sub-wave alongside FPV-05. Same for FPV-11: give it its own wave after FPV-09, or split FPV-09 so the manifest part lands before FPV-11.

findings.claim: FPV-05 and FPV-06 both consume the required-vs-informational claim model but neither depends on the other and both sit in phase 2, so they can be built in parallel against divergent claim semantics.
findings.evidence: issues/forgeplan/FPV-06.md:22 defines the model — 'required и informational claims' — and :25 '`R_eff = min(required_claim_scores)`'. issues/forgeplan/FPV-05.md:37 asserts an AC that presupposes it: 'Refuting Evidence fails its required claim.' manifest.json:56-60 gives FPV-05 depends ['FPV-02','FPV-03','FPV-04']; manifest.json:64-71 gives FPV-06 depends ['FPV-02'] — no edge between them, both phase 2. Neither AC references the field the pack's own draft already commits: protocol/schemas/work-contract.schema.json:172-190 places 'claim' and 'required' inside the acceptance item.
findings.recommendation: Add an explicit dependency in one direction (FPV-05 → FPV-06 is the natural one, since verification consumes the scoring semantics), or hoist the claim-model definition wholly into FPV-02 and make both FPV-05 and FPV-06 cite work-contract.schema.json's acceptance[].required as the binding definition.

findings.claim: FPV-08 declares high-level operations that are implemented by FPV-03/04/05, but depends only on FPV-02; it also silently redefines four already-shipped CLI commands with no compatibility or migration section.
findings.evidence: issues/forgeplan/FPV-08.md:27 'High-level operations: `next`, `context`, `contract`, `claim`, `execution`, `evidence`, `verify`, `status`, `search`.' manifest.json:87-93 gives FPV-08 '"depends": ["FPV-02"]' only, while `contract` is FPV-03, `execution` is FPV-04 and `evidence`/`verify` are FPV-05 — all same-phase siblings, so build order is unconstrained. Separately, `context`, `claim`, `status` and `search` already exist: crates/forgeplan-cli/src/commands/ contains context.rs, claim.rs, status.rs, search.rs and crates/forgeplan-cli/src/main.rs:410 declares `Context { ... }` (dispatched at main.rs:1260 as `commands::context::run(&id, json)` — the shipped command takes an id). FPV-08's heading list (F1) contains no Rollback/migration or Non-goals section covering the redefinition.
findings.recommendation: Add FPV-03/FPV-04/FPV-05 to FPV-08's depends, or split FPV-08 into a phase-1 parity slice (closing #304/#353/#374/#397) and a later phase-2/3 slice that adds the contract/execution/evidence/verify operations. Add a compatibility section naming which of the four existing commands change signature and what the deprecation path is.

findings.claim: FPV-02's acceptance criterion that unknown optional fields survive round-trips is directly contradicted by the pack's own draft schemas, which set additionalProperties:false at the root and at every nested level.
findings.evidence: issues/forgeplan/FPV-02.md:42 '- [ ] Unknown optional fields survive supported round-trips where required.' Against that: grep -n additionalProperties protocol/schemas/*.json shows 'false' at the root of all five schemas (work-contract.schema.json:6, execution-receipt.schema.json:6, evidence-bundle.schema.json:6, verification-verdict.schema.json:6, extension-manifest.schema.json:6) plus 20 further nested 'false' occurrences (e.g. work-contract.schema.json:67,71,90,106,142,164,188,211,248). The only escape hatch is a single top-level 'extensions' object (work-contract.schema.json:250, execution-receipt.schema.json:141, evidence-bundle.schema.json:176, verification-verdict.schema.json:91), which handles namespaced provider payloads (FPV-04) but not 'unknown optional fields' of core types.
findings.recommendation: Resolve the contract explicitly: either drop the round-trip criterion and state that Protocol v1 is strict-closed with the namespaced 'extensions' bag as the sole forward-compat channel, or relax additionalProperties on designated envelope levels and add a fixture proving preservation. As written, the first implementer must guess, and the guess is load-bearing for every adapter.

findings.claim: FPV-02 requires versioned schema IDs for 11 protocol types, but only 5 drafts exist; 6 types have no draft at all, and the manifest concept is split across three different names owned by three different issues.
findings.evidence: issues/forgeplan/FPV-02.md:16-26 lists ArtifactReference, ActorIdentity, Claim/Lease reference, WorkContract, ExecutionReceipt, EvidenceBundle, VerificationVerdict, AuthorityPolicy, ExternalReference, CapabilityManifest, ErrorEnvelope; FPV-02.md:40 '- [ ] Every type has a versioned schema ID.' protocol/schemas/ contains exactly five files: work-contract, execution-receipt, evidence-bundle, verification-verdict, extension-manifest. Missing drafts: ArtifactReference, ActorIdentity, Claim/Lease, AuthorityPolicy, ExternalReference, ErrorEnvelope. Naming split: FPV-02.md:25 says 'CapabilityManifest'; FPV-09.md:12 says 'Create CapabilityManifest' with AC :39 'Manifest schema is published under Protocol v1'; FPV-11.md:26 says 'extension manifest implementation'; the only shipped draft is titled 'ForgePlan Extension Manifest v1' ($id .../extension-manifest.v1.json).
findings.recommendation: Decide whether CapabilityManifest and Extension Manifest are one artifact or two, and name the single owning issue. Then either draft the 6 missing schemas inside FPV-02's scope or move them to a named follow-up so FPV-02's 'every type' criterion is achievable at close time.

findings.claim: GitHub issue #328 is claimed for closure by two different issues, creating conflicting closure ownership that ISSUE-GOVERNANCE's completion rule cannot resolve.
findings.evidence: issues/forgeplan/FPV-05.md:42 '- [ ] Existing #360 and #328 are closed or explicitly superseded by this implementation.' issues/forgeplan/FPV-06.md:37 '- [ ] Existing #325, #329 and relevant #328 scope are closed or superseded.' Both are phase 2 with no dependency edge between them (manifest.json:56-71). #328 confirmed OPEN: `gh issue view 328` → '#328 [OPEN] Core-side Evidence Decay enforcement: parse ADR Compliance section, surface fire...'. ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:36-44 makes 'related old issues closed/superseded' a hard close condition, so whichever issue finishes second cannot satisfy its own AC.
findings.recommendation: Split #328 explicitly: assign the decay *enforcement gate* to FPV-05 and the decay *scoring contribution* to FPV-06 with distinct AC wording, or give sole ownership to one and have the other reference it as context only. All eight referenced issues (#304 #325 #328 #329 #353 #360 #374 #397) are currently OPEN and correctly covered across FPV-05/06/08 — #328 is the only double-claim.

findings.claim: The entire pack is untracked in git, yet the issue-creation script writes a repo-relative pointer to it into the epic body — every created GitHub issue would reference a path that exists on no branch.
findings.evidence: `git ls-files docs/vnext | wc -l` → 0; `git status --porcelain docs/vnext` → '?? docs/vnext/'. scripts/create_github_issues.py:128-131 appends to the master body: 'See `docs/vnext/engineering-contract-layer/governance/EXECUTION-ORDER.md` in the implementation pack.' The same script writes its state file to ROOT/'.created-issues.json' (create_github_issues.py:25, :243) inside the same untracked tree, so the created-issue → key mapping that next_issue.py depends on is also unversioned and machine-local.
findings.recommendation: Commit the pack (and gitignore .created-issues.json, or move it out of the pack) before running create_github_issues.py. Creating 16 public issues that point at an uncommitted local directory is not reversible cheaply — the bodies would need a second pass to fix.

findings.claim: Seven of the sixteen issues are multi-issue programs in a single body, contradicting the pack's own one-issue-one-PR rule.
findings.evidence: governance/AGENTS-VNEXT.md 'PR size: Одна issue — один основной PR.' Against that: FPV-12 carries three separate deliverable sections plus a fourth workstream (FPV-12.md:14-24 'Cursor deliverables / Codex deliverables / OpenCode deliverables', :12 'plus normalize the existing Claude Code integration'); FPV-13 covers four orchestrators plus a generic SDK (FPV-13.md:22-27); FPV-15 scopes nine subsystems (FPV-15.md:16-24: HTTP MCP, auth, event ingestion, audit log, multi-repo registry, webhooks, OpenTelemetry, replay/recovery, remote evidence refs); FPV-02 requires 11 protocol types (FPV-02.md:16-26); FPV-08 bundles 6 role profiles + 9 operations + closure of 4 existing issues + a latency benchmark (FPV-08.md:16-27); FPV-10 bundles README + website IA + generated references + CI example tests + EN/RU parity (FPV-10.md:23-30); FPV-14 adds 6 new view families (FPV-14.md:16-22).
findings.recommendation: Split at least FPV-12 (one issue per host, per EXECUTION-ORDER.md:37 which already says 'Implement one reference adapter first, preferably OpenCode'), FPV-13 (one per orchestrator), and FPV-15 (transport+auth vs ingestion+replay vs observability). AGENTS-VNEXT's own Stop condition 'dependency не завершена' will otherwise fire mid-issue with no place to record partial completion.
findings.location: governance/AGENTS-VNEXT.md (PR size) vs issues/marketplace/FPV-12.md:14-24, issues/marketplace/FPV-13.md:22-27, issues/forgeplan/FPV-15.md:16-24

findings.claim: A significant fraction of acceptance criteria are prose aspirations with no machine-checkable oracle; the two performance criteria have no numeric target anywhere in the pack.
findings.evidence: Untestable as written: FPV-08.md:36 '- [ ] MCP cold/warm latency benchmark and budget are added.' — `grep -rn 'ms\b|p95|latency|budget' architecture/` returns only prose mentions (08-AGENT-API-AND-MCP.md:47 '#304 MCP latency'), no number, so 'budget' has no value to assert against. FPV-14.md:36 '- [ ] Large-workspace performance budget and fixtures exist.' — same, no number. FPV-12.md:34 '- [ ] Unsupported capabilities are reported honestly.' — 'honestly' has no oracle. FPV-01.md:37 '- [ ] Architecture dependency rules are enforceable by crate/module tests or lint where practical.' — 'where practical' makes it unfalsifiable; FPV-01.md:38 '- [ ] EN/RU canonical documents are structurally aligned.' — 'structurally aligned' undefined. FPV-10.md:36 '- [ ] Methodology acronyms are not required to understand the homepage.' — subjective; FPV-10.md:12 objective 'understandable in under one minute' — unmeasured. FPV-09.md:43 '- [ ] Website/Marketplace compatibility matrix can be generated from results.' — 'can be' is weaker than 'is'. FPV-11.md:42 '- [ ] Claude-specific agents/commands/hooks are clearly marked.' — 'clearly'. FPV-14.md:33 '- [ ] External task/workspace/session/PR/CI links render safely.' — 'safely' undefined. FPV-00 has no checkbox list at all, only prose 'Definition of Done' asserting 'cross-host semantic portability test passes' — no such test is defined in any issue or architecture doc.
findings.recommendation: Attach a concrete oracle to each: numeric p50/p95 targets for FPV-08 and FPV-14 (reuse the numbers in issue #304 rather than inventing new ones); replace 'honestly'/'clearly'/'safely' with the specific check (manifest field must equal conformance result; link scheme allowlist; marker present in catalog JSON); define the cross-host portability test in FPV-09 and reference it by name from FPV-00's DoD.

findings.claim: The pack's own validator checks only file existence and dependency-key resolution — it cannot detect any of the defect classes the governance document defines, so the pack passes its gate while violating its contract.
findings.evidence: scripts/validate_pack.py:5-26 checks: eight required files exist (:5-13), issue keys are unique (:17), each key has a body (:19), each dependency name resolves to a known key (:20-21), each key has a readable .md (:22-23), and each schema file parses as JSON (:24-25). It never checks required sections (F1), never detects cycles or forward phase dependencies (F2/F4), never diffs the .md bodies against bodies.json, and never cross-checks EXECUTION-ORDER.md against manifest phases. Running it on the current pack prints 'OK: 16 issues, 5 schemas, prompts and governance present' despite every finding above.
findings.recommendation: Add to validate_pack.py: (a) required-section assertion per bodies.json entry, (b) topological sort with cycle detection, (c) assertion that dep.phase < issue.phase (or an explicit same-phase allowlist), (d) byte-diff of each issues/<repo>/<KEY>.md tail against bodies[KEY].body, (e) cross-check that every FPV key named in EXECUTION-ORDER.md appears in a wave consistent with its manifest phase.

findings.claim: next_issue.py fails open: with `gh` absent or unauthenticated it treats every issue as incomplete and confidently reports FPV-01 as the next unblocked task instead of erroring.
findings.evidence: scripts/next_issue.py: `def closed(repo, number): if shutil.which('gh') is None: return False` and `p=subprocess.run([...]); if p.returncode: return False`. Both failure paths return False, so `completed` stays empty, so the first issue whose deps are all 'incomplete-but-not-blocking' … actually the first child in (phase, key) order with empty `missing` is FPV-01, which is printed as `{'next': ...}` with no warning. The same happens when `.created-issues.json` is absent (`state={}`), which is the current state of the untracked pack (F10).
findings.recommendation: Make the gh-missing and gh-error paths raise or emit an explicit `{'next': null, 'error': 'gh unavailable — completion state unknown'}` rather than a confident FPV-01. As written it is a silent-failure generator of exactly the class CLAUDE.md RED LINE #5 warns about.

findings.claim: The label taxonomy that ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md defines is never applied by the issue-creation script, so all 16 issues land unlabeled and the priority/blocked/needs-decision routing is inert.
findings.evidence: governance/ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:3-21 defines 16 labels (area:protocol … needs:verification). scripts/create_github_issues.py:80-89 `create_issue` invokes `gh issue create --repo <repo> --title <title> --body-file -` with no `--label`, and `edit_issue` (:92-98) passes only `--body-file`. No other call site references labels; `grep -n label scripts/create_github_issues.py` yields nothing.
findings.recommendation: Add a `labels` array to each manifest.json entry and pass `--label` on create (and `--add-label` on edit), or delete the label section from ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md so it does not read as a shipped convention.

findings.claim: FPV-08's stated goal of reducing the MCP tool surface can trip the existing CI drift detector with a misleading failure message.
findings.evidence: issues/manifest.json:92 summarises FPV-08 as 'Reduce tool surface, add batch context ...'. /Users/explosovebit/Work/ForgePlan/scripts/check-mcp-tool-count.sh:53-58: `ACTUAL=$(grep -cE '^[[:space:]]*#\[tool\(' "$SERVER_RS")` then `if [[ "$ACTUAL" -lt 30 ]]; then echo "FAIL: cannot find MCP tools в $SERVER_RS (found $ACTUAL — expected ≥30)"; echo "      Has rmcp tool macro contract changed? Update this script."; exit 2; fi`. Current count is 73 per CLAUDE.md; a role-profile consolidation to the 9 high-level operations named in FPV-08.md:27 would fall well under 30 and produce a wrong diagnosis.
findings.recommendation: Add a line to FPV-08 (or its Rollback/migration section once F1 is fixed) noting that scripts/check-mcp-tool-count.sh's `-lt 30` floor must be lowered in the same PR that reduces the surface.

findings.claim: FPV-12's acceptance criteria require artifacts produced by FPV-04 and FPV-05, which it does not declare as dependencies — satisfiable only through the transitive edge via FPV-09.
findings.evidence: issues/marketplace/FPV-12.md:33 '- [ ] ExecutionReceipt and EvidenceBundle are submitted in canonical schemas.' manifest.json:133-140 gives FPV-12 '"depends": ["FPV-03", "FPV-07", "FPV-09", "FPV-11"]' — neither FPV-04 (ExecutionReceipt) nor FPV-05 (EvidenceBundle). It happens to work only because manifest.json:99-105 gives FPV-09 depends on FPV-04 and FPV-05. Any future reordering that loosens FPV-09 silently unblocks FPV-12 against unimplemented types.
findings.recommendation: Add FPV-04 and FPV-05 to FPV-12's depends. The DAG is otherwise sound: verified acyclic, and no issue depends on anything in a strictly later phase.

findings.claim: Consistency check between the 16 individual .md files and bodies.json: the body text is byte-identical for all 16, so no drift exists today — but neither file is a faithful mirror of what will be posted to GitHub, and nothing enforces the match.
findings.evidence: Programmatic diff of each issues/<repo>/<KEY>.md tail (after the first '---' separator) against bodies[KEY]['body'] reports `md_body_matches_bodies.json=True` for all of FPV-00..FPV-15, with title and repo also matching manifest.json in every case. Divergence is structural only: the .md files carry a header block ('- **Repository:** / **Phase:** / **Dependencies:** / **Summary:**', e.g. FPV-05.md:3-6) that bodies.json omits, while the posted GitHub body gains a generated '## Program Links' section (create_github_issues.py:101-113) that neither file contains. validate_pack.py performs no such diff (F13), so future edits to one file will not be caught.
findings.recommendation: Generate the .md files from bodies.json + manifest.json rather than maintaining both by hand, and include the Program Links block in the generated .md so the in-repo artifact matches the posted issue.

findings.claim: Dependency DAG structural verdict: acyclic, all dependencies resolvable, no forward (later-phase) edges — but four same-phase edges mean 'phase' is not a parallelism unit, and FPV-00 is an isolated node.
findings.evidence: From issues/manifest.json: FPV-00(p0,[]), FPV-01(p0,[]), FPV-02(p1,[01]), FPV-03(p2,[02]), FPV-04(p2,[02]), FPV-05(p2,[02,03,04]), FPV-06(p2,[02]), FPV-07(p2,[02,03]), FPV-08(p2,[02]), FPV-09(p3,[02,03,04,05,07]), FPV-10(p1,[01]), FPV-11(p3,[02,09]), FPV-12(p4,[03,07,09,11]), FPV-13(p5,[04,05,09,11]), FPV-14(p5,[02,03,04,05,07]), FPV-15(p6,[02,04,05,07,09]). No dep.phase exceeds issue.phase; four edges are same-phase (05→03, 05→04, 07→03, 11→09). FPV-00 has no dependents and no dependencies — nothing in the manifest expresses that it is the umbrella (that relationship exists only in create_github_issues.py's MASTER_KEY constant, line 26).
findings.recommendation: Either subdivide phase 2 and phase 3 so phases are genuinely parallel batches, or rename the field to 'wave-group' and stop treating it as an ordering guarantee. Consider adding an explicit 'parent': 'FPV-00' field to the manifest so the epic relationship is data rather than a script constant.

area: Issue-backlog coordination: 16 proposed FPV issues vs 32 open ForgePlan/forgeplan + 1 marketplace + 2 forgeplan-web issues
summary: All 8 issues named in ISSUE-GOVERNANCE.md:48 (#304, #325, #328, #329, #353, #360, #374, #397) ARE referenced by name in the FPV bodies — the hypothesis that one was silently dropped does not hold, and I report that as a negative result. area: Factual-premise verification: vNext pack claims about today's ForgePlan
summary: I verified every factual assertion the pack makes about current ForgePlan against the codebase, the 18 active ADRs, the marketplace repo, and the forgeplan-web repo. Roughly half the premises hold; the load-bearing ones do not. The pack's canonical boundary ("core is never a coding agent, never owns agent processes, never a workflow engine") is contradicted by shipped code — `forgeplan-core` already spawns `claude --print --agent <name>` through its playbook dispatchers under ACTIVE ADR-011 — and the pack cites zero existing ADRs (grep for `ADR-[0-9]+` across the whole pack returns 0 hits), so nothing reconciles or supersedes ADR-001/ADR-009/ADR-010/ADR-011. FPV-01's premise that ForgePlan "is currently described as a project-management layer" is REFUTED (the docs say the literal opposite), while the real conflicting positioning — "agent harness" — lives in 22 published blog posts the pack never scopes. FPV-14's "Web remains read-only" is only true of the `/api/*` proxy: forgeplan-web already ships `@forgeplan/web-agent`, a Claude Agent SDK daemon the browser drives, i.e. the exact "agent launcher" FPV-14 forbids. A design pack whose boundary is stated against a repo state that no longer exists will generate work that either contradicts active decisions or silently regresses shipped features.

findings.claim: The pack's canonical product boundary asserts core is not a coding agent, does not own agent processes and is not a general-purpose workflow engine — but forgeplan-core already ships a playbook workflow executor that spawns `claude --print --agent <name>` subprocesses under ACTIVE ADR-011, and the pack cites zero existing ADRs so nothing supersedes it (REFUTED premise).

## Direct answers first

**1. Is the program itself something that must exist as an EPIC artifact? — YES, now, before FPV-01 opens.**
CLAUDE.md:248 routes "cross-team, strategy" to Critical depth = `Epic → PRD[] → Spec[] → RFC[] → ADR[]`. vNext is 16 issues / 3 repos / 7 phases — Critical by any reading. CLAUDE.md:184-185 is explicit: «`/smith` читает состояние через `forgeplan_health` / `forgeplan_claims` — пустой граф означает, что он маршрутизирует вслепую. Если работа велась, а артефактов не появилось, это дефект процесса, а не экономия.» Today `grep -rli 'vnext|workcontract' .forgeplan` returns nothing: a 16-issue program is invisible to `forgeplan_health`, `forgeplan_order` and the graph. That is the process defect the rule names. Precedent for an EPIC as program anchor: EPIC-007 "Playbook Runtime + Pack Marketplace" (`status: active`), which anchors PRD-065/066/067 shaped later — the EPIC came first, the PRDs followed per workstream. Do **not** mint 16 PRDs now: DUP-01 shows 13 of 15 executable FPV issues duplicate existing artifacts.

**2. The 01-PRODUCT-BOUNDARY / 02-TARGET-ARCHITECTURE question — answer is (c) both, with a hard ordering constraint.**
The precedent settles it. `docs/space-mesh/` shipped as **two commits**: `a4af8e6 docs(space-mesh): preserve research sources in-repo` (the 512-line handoff + 246 KB raw research JSON — durable *input material* under `docs/`), then `99d0cf0 docs(prd,adr,spec,evid): shape space-mesh cross-project layer` (PRD-081 + ADR-018 + SPEC-006 + EVID-148 in `.forgeplan/`, linked, `validate` PASS, **none activated**). The artifacts cite the docs/ paths as sources (EVID-148:196,214,220). That is exactly the split CLAUDE.md:174 demands: `docs/` = guides and source material, `.forgeplan/adrs/` = the decisions.

So: keep all 18 architecture docs in `docs/vnext/` as the rationale annex (option a), **and** mint the EPIC now (option b). But the canonical boundary ADR is **not** mintable today, and that is the finding that changes the placement plan: the boundary contradicts four ADRs I verified active myself — ADR-001 `status: active` (:10) "No adapter traits — AI agent is the orchestrator, not Forgeplan"; ADR-003 `status: active` (:8) "Markdown files as source of truth"; ADR-009 `status: active` (:11) "Forgeplan as orchestrator"; ADR-011 `status: active` (:8) "Plugin/Agent dispatchers invoke claude --print directly" — while `grep -rnoE 'ADR-[0-9]{3}' docs/vnext/` returns **0**. Minting a canonical ADR from these docs today would silently override four active decisions. The collision register must land as a Problem **first**; FPV-01's ADR then carries explicit `supersede` links. That ordering is why I split rows 1-2 into SPLIT rather than a straight CONVERT.

**3. `docs/schemas/` — no.** It holds six markdown files only (`PRD-SCHEMA.md`, `EPIC-SCHEMA.md`, `SPEC-SCHEMA.md` + `.ru` variants) — human documentation of validator contracts. Zero machine-readable schemas exist there or anywhere else in the repo (`find . -name '*.schema.json'` outside the pack hits only `website/.astro/` build cache). The five protocol schemas declare `"$id": "https://forgeplan.dev/schemas/work-contract.v1.json"` — their publication home is the **website**, not `docs/schemas/`. And they describe zero shipped code (`grep -rn WorkContract crates/` → 0). Promoting unimplemented drafts into the directory users read as normative validator contracts is advertising planned as shipped — the exact thing FPV-10's own "## Important" forbids. They stay pack-local until FPV-02 lands Rust DTOs.

**4. `/scripts/` — no.** `git ls-files "*.py"` returns **empty**: the repo has no Python anywhere, and `scripts/` holds six `.sh` files that are CI gates running on every PR (`check-mcp-tool-count.sh`, `smoke-test.sh`). The three pack scripts are program-scoped one-offs whose root resolution is `Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1]` = the pack root (validate_pack.py:4); moving them breaks that and introduces a Python toolchain to a repo with no Python lint, no CI wiring, no convention. They stay. What must change is `.created-issues.json` (create_github_issues.py:25) — machine-local state written **inside** a tracked tree.

**5. `ref/` — does not fit the `dev/` rule; delete the duplicate, preserve the provenance.** The `.gitignore` rule reads "`dev/` reference clones — external repos studied as prior art, not ours to track" and enumerates five third-party repos (`dev/vibe-kanban/`, `dev/gastown/`, …). The vNext pack is **ours** — ForgePlan's own program design authored for this repo — so it fails the "external, not ours" test, same as `sources/`. I verified by content, not by name (per the space-mesh discipline, which committed the handoff only after "verified by md5"): `diff -rq ref/.../payload/docs/vnext/ docs/vnext/` → **no output**, and the PR template diff → **exit 0**. The payload is byte-identical; the zip is an archive of the same directory (79 entries / 61 files). Eight files were never imported (`01-IMPORT-MAP.md` itself says `PROMPT-START-AGENT.md` "Не копируется"), and `PROGRAM-COORDINATOR.md:13-14` still instructs running `./scripts/install.sh` from the archive — which exists only in an untracked, un-ignored directory that one `git clean -fdx` erases. Move those eight into the pack; delete the rest.

**6. `.github/PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` — GitHub-valid, shadows nothing, but inert.** Verified: no `.github/pull_request_template.md`, no root-level, no `docs/` template — this repo had **no** PR template at all before. So it shadows nothing. But a `PULL_REQUEST_TEMPLATE/` *directory* with no default sibling is opt-in only: GitHub applies it solely via `?template=forgeplan-vnext.md` / `gh pr create --template`, and `grep -rniE 'pull_request_template|--template' docs/vnext/` returns 0 — no agent will pass it. Keep the placement (promoting a 43-line vNext-specific form to repo default would impose it on every docs/chore/release PR); fix the pack to name the invocation.

**Not a placement, but adjacent:** `.serena/` is also untracked and un-ignored (`git status`) and will be swept into any `git add .` alongside the pack. Decide it separately before the first commit.

summary:
Twenty-one loss vectors found. Three are BLOCKERs: the entire vNext pack exists ONLY as untracked files — both the installed copy (`docs/vnext/`, 60 files, 240K) and the source (`ref/`, 384K + 90K zip) — and `git log --all -- 'docs/vnext' 'ref/'` returns empty, proving neither has ever been committed on any branch. A single `git clean -fd` destroys the whole program. Same for PROB-080/PROB-081: two complete, high-quality artifacts (186 and 124 lines) that exist nowhere in git history and whose only other copy is the gitignored, derived LanceDB index.

Working-tree state verified: current branch `docs/ddr-terminology-alignment` is `0` ahead / `12` behind `origin/dev`, and `git merge-base --is-ancestor HEAD origin/dev` succeeds — the branch's own work (PR #406) is already merged; what remains uncommitted here is unrelated to DDR. The `+86` CLAUDE.md diff is the finished "Task List Discipline" doctrine (the "nothing gets lost" rules themselves), and the PROB-047 diff is a one-byte trailing-newline artifact of a direct write. A bootstrap branch cut from HEAD would carry both along AND miss 12 commits including the merged Memory-graph-citizen work (#412, PR bbfd02f) that fixes defects PROB-080 documents.

Content verification performed rather than assumed: `diff -rq ref/.../payload/docs/vnext docs/vnext` exits 0 (byte-identical) and `shasum -a 256 -c CHECKSUMS.sha256` reports 0 non-OK lines, so the only unique material in `ref/` is 9 pack-meta/script files plus the archive — that is what must be preserved, not the 60 duplicated payload files.

Two feared vectors were checked and largely cleared, and I am reporting them as cleared rather than inflating them: the scan-import PROB-047 landmine is NOT live (mitigation 1 is implemented at `crates/forgeplan-core/src/scan/detect.rs:80-85`, and no pack file trips Tier 3), and the CI frontmatter gate will not block PROB-080/081 — but only because that gate is itself inert, which is its own finding.

The structural loss is that the whole 16-issue program has zero representation in the forgeplan graph: `grep -rlniE 'vnext|FPV-0|WorkContract' .forgeplan/` is empty, and across 60+ pack files exactly ONE existing artifact ID is referenced (PRD-073). Meanwhile FPV-01 re-opens decisions already recorded in active ADR-001 and ADR-009, and directs the canonical boundary document to `docs/architecture/product-boundary.md` — contradicting CLAUDE.md's rule that decisions live only in `.forgeplan/adrs/`.
